items.title: Leonant Yert retains position as Most Outstanding PR Agency
items.description: Leonant Yert Ltd has been named the “Most Outstanding Public Relations Agency (PR Consultancy of the Year)” for the 2025 review period at the 2026 Institute of Public Relations (IPR), PR Ghana Excellence Awards. This latest recognition strengthens Leonant Yert’s position as the leading Public Relations consultancy in Ghana and validates the Firm’s previous winning of the same award for the 2023-2024 review period. The back-to-back recognition also underscores the Consultancy’s commitment to delivering strategic communication, reputation management, issues and crisis management and stakeholder engagement solutions that create measurable value for its clients. According to the IPR’s Professional Awards Committee, Leonant Yert’s selection as the best was based on its exceptional work, demonstrated through strategic leadership and measurable results delivered during the review period. The award was received by Isaac Kusi and Alberta James, both Account Managers of the Firm at the recently concluded 2026 National Public Relations Summit and Awards in Koforidua. The event which was held under the theme, “Public Relations and Leadership Readiness” brought together public relations practitioners, corporate leaders and other stakeholders to examine the evolving role of the profession and recognise excellence in communication practice. The annual PR Excellence Awards is IPR Ghana’s platform for recognising exceptional work, encouraging continuous improvement and strengthening the public relations profession in Ghana. The Awards highlight achievements across PR consultancies, independent practitioners, corporate communications teams, government agencies, NGOs and other organisations. Speaking on this achievement, Chief Executive Officer and Account Team Lead at Leonant Yert, Nii Okai Nunoo said, “retaining the Most Outstanding Public Relations Agency award, is testimony to the great collaboration that exists between our clients and us and also within our team. It also shows the commitment and diligence that we at Leonant Yert and our clients have invested in developing and executing solutions which improve our clients’ performance and reputation and ultimately give the stakeholders of our various clients the assurance they need.” “At Leonant Yert, we believe that true value is built when organisations demonstrate reliability through their actions. Our role is to help bridge the gap between what organisations say and do and what their stakeholders experience; giving stakeholders tangible reasons to be confident and assured of our clients’ reliability and guaranteeing the expected outcomes”, he added. Mr Nunoo expressed gratitude to Leonant Yert’s clients and partners for their continued confidence and support, describing their trust as an important part of the Firm’s success. Established in 2016, Leonant Yert is a multiple award winning public relations and communications firm providing a full-suite service within Ghana and with the capability to undertake projects across the rest of Africa. Leonant Yert operates under the brand promise “building true value”, with an emphasis on improving assurance for its clients, through trust, collaboration, creativity, and professional service. The Firm’s signature offering focuses on protecting, building, and projecting the business and reputation of its clients. This covers the key service areas of business support, public policy, and organisational effectiveness. Through its work, Leonant Yert supports corporate entities, individuals and organisations to navigate communication challenges, strengthen stakeholder relationships, build credible, trusted reputations and ultimately improve corporate performance. Its approach focuses on ensuring that communication and engagement deliver more than visibility by helping clients demonstrate value, manage risks, maintain stakeholder confidence and remain prepared when outcomes matter.

items.title: Tinubu defends borrowing plans, says investments ‘ll expand opportunities for future generations
items.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA —PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has responded to criticism, especially from opposition leaders, over new loans the country has accessed from international institutions and banks. ‎ ‎In an essay titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” to be published on Nigerian news platforms, President Tinubu wrote: “The real question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, what value we create and what future we leave behind.” ‎ ‎He identified the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid upgrades and the modernisation of key commercial ports in Lagos as major projects expected to strengthen Nigeria’s productive capacity. ‎ ‎The President said the projects, alongside investments in healthcare, education and vocational training, would connect economic regions, reduce logistics costs, unlock agricultural and industrial potential and attract private investment. ‎ ‎The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is expected to cut logistics costs along its corridor by 15 to 20 per cent. It could add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s GDP through expanded trade, tourism, and industrial activity. ‎ ‎The project is also projected to generate about 100,000 direct jobs in construction and engineering, alongside more than 150,000 indirect jobs in logistics, materials and related services. ‎ ‎According to him: “We are not simply building highways. We are opening economic corridors, connecting markets, unlocking industries and reshaping Nigeria’s economic geography.” ‎ ‎He said the administration’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2030 would require sustained infrastructure investment to support higher productivity, industrialisation and trade. ‎ ‎“We cannot build a USD 1 trillion economy with infrastructure designed for an economy a fraction of that size,” Tinubu said. ‎ ‎He wrote that improving economic indicators and growing international investor confidence are creating opportunities for Nigeria to attract long-term investment and expand critical infrastructure. ‎ ‎The President said the economic reforms his administration introduced in May 2023 helped restore macroeconomic stability, strengthen public finances, and improve the country’s standing in international financial markets. ‎ ‎He said a $1 trillion economy would not emerge by declaration alone but must be built through sustained investment, higher productivity, industrialisation, and trade, stressing that infrastructure development would be critical to achieving the target by 2030. ‎ ‎In an article titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier. ‎ ‎He also said gross external reserves rose to $55.1 billion as of October 9, 2026, including about $46 billion in net reserves, while the tax-to-GDP ratio increased to 12.5 per cent from seven per cent. ‎ ‎Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier. ‎ ‎The President attributed the improvements to measures including petrol subsidy removal, exchange rate unification, tax reforms and coordinated efforts to tackle inflation. ‎ ‎“The decisions taken since 2023 were difficult but necessary,” he said, referring to the reforms. ‎ ‎Tinubu said the gains have strengthened Nigeria’s ability to attract investment and finance projects that support long-term economic growth. ‎ ‎“Confidence has a price; our cost of borrowing is going down, and the country risk premium has drastically decreased,” he said. ‎ ‎The President cited positive assessments by international credit rating agencies as evidence of improved confidence in the economy. ‎ ‎ ‎“These are not political endorsements; they are independent assessments by global rating agencies, index providers, regulators and investors, recognising stronger external reserves, improved macroeconomic management and greater financial credibility,” Tinubu said. ‎ ‎According to the President, the improved standing could help Nigeria attract more institutional investors, secure longer-term financing and reduce borrowing costs. ‎ ‎He said the administration was shifting public borrowing away from financing short-term fiscal pressures towards investments that would generate economic returns, create jobs and expand opportunities for future generations. ‎ ‎The President said the government was also pursuing longer-term financing arrangements to match the lifespan of infrastructure assets, reduce refinancing pressures and secure more competitive funding for productive investments. ‎ ‎President Tinubu said Nigeria must convert renewed international confidence into capital expenditure, completed infrastructure and lasting economic benefits for citizens. ‎ ‎He identified five priorities for the next phase of the Federal Executive Council’s economic strategy: food affordability and energy price stability; budget harmonisation and fiscal discipline; completion of high-impact projects and investment in critical infrastructure; an improved economic policy framework and regulatory efficiency; and targeted household support alongside investment in human development. ‎ ‎The President stressed that the success of the current administration’s economic schemes would be measured by completed projects, increased investment, employment generation and improved living standards. ‎ ‎“Securing financing is not the achievement. Completing the project, delivering value and improving the lives of Nigerians is the achievement,” he said. ‎ ‎He added that the nation’s economic ambition must be supported by responsible borrowing and investments that create lasting opportunities for future generations. The post Tinubu defends borrowing plans, says investments ‘ll expand opportunities for future generations appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Province du Kourittenga : une conférence publique pour promouvoir les idéaux de la RPP
items.description: La province du Kourittenga a organisé une conférence publique provinciale, le jeudi 29 octobre 2026 à Koupèla, sur le civisme, la citoyenneté, l’engagement patriotique, la culture de la paix et les idéaux de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP). La conférence publique provinciale sur le civisme, la citoyenneté, l’engagement patriotique, la culture de la paix et les idéaux de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP) a connu la participation des autorités administratives, religieuses et coutumières, ainsi que des représentants des différentes couches sociales de la province. Elle visait à renforcer les connaissances des populations sur les valeurs citoyennes, le patriotisme, la cohésion sociale et les orientations de la RPP. Trois communications, animées par des personnes ressources, ont ensuite permis d’aborder les différents sous-thèmes retenus. Prenant la parole, Egède Magloir Koudougou, conseiller en droits humains et conférencier, a souligné l’importance de faire connaître aux populations les idéaux de la RPP et de les amener à se les approprier. Pour illustrer son propos, il a rappelé ce proverbe : « Si tu dors dans la natte de quelqu’un, tu dors à terre ». A travers cette image, le conférencier a invité les citoyens à comprendre la nécessité de compter sur leurs propres efforts, de valoriser les ressources nationales et de s’impliquer dans la construction du pays. Pour sa part, le directeur général de la promotion de la citoyenneté et de la paix, Benjamin Sow, a mis l’accent sur le rôle de la conscience citoyenne dans la construction d’une nation unie et résiliente. Selon lui, la reconquête du territoire doit nécessairement s’accompagner de la reconquête des consciences. Il a ainsi appelé les populations à s’engager davantage dans la lutte contre les comportements inciviques, à promouvoir la paix et la solidarité et à faire preuve de responsabilité dans leurs communautés. Il a également insisté sur la responsabilité individuelle et collective dans la promotion du civisme, du respect des règles communes et de l’engagement patriotique. « La reconquête du territoire doit aller de pair avec celle des consciences », a-t-il dit. Traduire les valeurs en actes concrets Le parrain de la conférence, le commandant de la deuxième région militaire, Lassané Porgo a, quant à lui, invité les citoyens à accompagner les initiatives portées par le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Il a insisté sur l’importance de la mobilisation citoyenne, du patriotisme et de la discipline dans la réalisation des objectifs nationaux. Il a exhorté les participants à traduire les valeurs évoquées au cours de la conférence en actes concrets dans leur quotidien, notamment par le respect des institutions, la solidarité et la contribution aux efforts de développement du Burkina. Présidant la conférence, le haut-commissaire de la province du Kourittenga, Moctar Ilboudo, a salué la forte mobilisation des autorités et des populations autour de cette initiative. Il a exprimé sa reconnaissance à l’ensemble des acteurs ayant contribué à l’organisation de l’activité. Le premier responsable de la province a invité les participants à s’approprier les enseignements des différentes communications et à les mettre en pratique dans leurs familles, leurs lieux de travail et leurs communautés. Il a également souligné l’importance de l’engagement de tous dans la promotion du civisme, de la paix, de la cohésion sociale et du développement local. La conférence publique provinciale s’est achevée par une plantation d’arbres, un geste symbolique traduisant l’engagement citoyen des participants en faveur de la préservation de l’environnement et du développement durable. Amédéé Wend-La-Sida SELGA

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026: au Sénégal, les jeunes femmes aussi pratiquent la lutte, sport le plus populaire du pays [5/5]
items.description: Samedi 31 octobre, s'ouvrent les premiers Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse sur le continent africain. Ce sera à Dakar où, pendant 15 jours, 2 700 athlètes de plus de 200 pays disputeront 25 disciplines en compétition officielle. Parmi les compétitions où le Sénégal est particulièrement attendu : la lutte, sport le plus populaire du pays. Si tout le monde connaît la lutte traditionnelle pratiquée par les hommes, il existe aussi une équipe nationale de femmes lutteuses. Pour ces JOJ, qui imposent la parité pour chacune des disciplines, quatre Sénégalaises de moins de 18 ans défendront donc les couleurs du Sénégal.

items.title: Women Should Never Give Birth in Shackles
items.description: Click to expand Image A woman in Australia. © 2008 Getty Images An incarcerated Indigenous woman was reportedly shackled during a hospital stay earlier this month to deliver her baby by caesarean section in a Queensland hospital in Australia. Queensland Corrective Services promised an internal review but did not confirm the shackling. Shackling a woman during childbirth contravenes international human rights standards. The incident happened days before Australia’s two major political parties blocked a vote in parliament on October 14 on a bill to ban the shackling of prisoners during childbirth. United Nations human rights experts criticized the Australian parliament’s failure to vote on the bill. Prisoners and detainees do not lose their rights to health or to be treated humanely and with dignity. Restraining a woman during childbirth raises grave concerns about degrading treatment and interference with care, which constitute obstetric violence. Obstetric violence is the physical and emotional abuse of pregnant people seeking sexual and reproductive health services and information, including maternal health. It is a form of gender-based violence and a violation of fundamental human rights. As a UN member state, Australia has endorsed the Bangkok Rules, a UN resolution that sets out minimum standards for the treatment of women in prison. The resolution specifically prohibits the use of restraints on women during labor, birth or immediately after birth. The well-being of the mother and the needs of her newborn should take priority over punitive practices. Australian authorities should investigate who authorized the shackling, whether clinicians objected and how those objections were handled. There should be accountability for any wrongdoing and an effective remedy for the woman. She should have independent legal advice and support, without pressure to disclose her experience or identity publicly. The Australian government should also promptly adopt consistent national safeguards and prohibit the practice of shackling prisoners in labor. It should introduce reforms that outline appropriate hospital and prison protocols for pregnant women, staff training, rapid escalation for clinicians, and independent monitoring. A prison sentence must never be a justification for woman to give birth without dignity.

items.title: Immersion à Simandou : de l’extraction du minerai au chargement des trains, des journalistes découvrent les coulisses des opérations menées par Rio Tinto Simfer
items.description: Des journalistes issus de différents médias guinéens ont effectué les 28 et 29 octobre, une immersion sur le site minier de Simandou. Cette visite de terrain initiée par Rio Tinto Simfer, détenteur des blocs 3 et 4 du projet Simandou leur a permis de découvrir les différentes étapes du processus d’exploitation du minerai de fer, depuis les travaux géologiques et l’extraction jusqu’au traitement et au chargement des wagons destinés à acheminer la production vers le port de Morebaya, dans la préfecture de Forécariah. Au cœur de la chaîne de montagnes de Simandou, dans le sud-est de la Guinée, les journalistes ont pu découvrir de près les installations et les différentes opérations qui permettent de valoriser l'un des plus importants gisements de minerai de fer au monde. Cette immersion de deux jours avait pour objectif de permettre aux professionnels des médias de mieux comprendre le fonctionnement du projet, à travers les explications de plusieurs responsables et techniciens intervenant dans les différentes étapes de la chaîne de production. Zézé Kalivogui, surintendant de la géologie minière, a expliqué les particularités qui font de Simandou un gisement exceptionnel. « C'est un gisement de classe mondiale. Et le processus qui a contribué à la mise en place de ce gisement exceptionnel est un processus naturel d'enrichissement supergène », a-t-il expliqué. Selon lui, au cours de millions d'années, l'altération météorique et la circulation des eaux souterraines ont favorisé le lessivage des formations ferrifères, entraînant l'élimination de certaines impuretés, notamment la silice et l'aluminium. Revenant sur l'historique des recherches géologiques, il a indiqué que Rio Tinto a acquis le permis en 1997. Depuis, d'importants travaux de recherche ont été réalisés sur l'ensemble de la chaîne montagneuse, longue d’environ 100 kilomètres. Ces travaux ont notamment porté sur la cartographie détaillée, les levés géophysiques et les activités de forage. « À date, on peut estimer la totalité des forages réalisés à plus de 400 kilomètres », a-t-il précisé, comparant cette distance à celle qui sépare l'est et l'ouest de la Guinée. Il a également expliqué que les opérations de forage s'accompagnent d'un important travail d'échantillonnage et d'analyse. Tous les deux mètres, des échantillons sont prélevés afin de faire l'objet d'études détaillées. Sabaty, un centre de formation au service des compétences locales Au centre de formation Sabaty, les journalistes ont découvert les dispositifs mis en place pour former les travailleurs aux différents métiers et aux exigences opérationnelles du projet. Mamadi Condé, surintendant formation au niveau de Simfer, qui assure également l'intérim du manager formation, a présenté les différentes composantes de cette infrastructure. D'après ses explications, le centre forme par semaine entre 500 et 700 apprenants venus des zones de communautés impactés et admis de différentes concours. Il comprend plusieurs espaces dédiés à l'apprentissage pratique et théorique. Parmi ses équipements figurent six cabines de simulation destinées à familiariser les travailleurs avec la conduite de différents engins. Il s'agit notamment de deux cabines simulateurs de chargeuses, deux de camions, une d'excavateur et une d’élévateur Toyota. Une cabine destinée à la simulation de conduite de bulldozer est également en cours de conception. Le centre dispose aussi d'un espace de démonstration des risques professionnels. Celui-ci permet aux travailleurs d'être confrontés aux situations dangereuses avant leur intervention sur le terrain et de découvrir les mesures de prévention et de contrôle appropriées. À cela s'ajoutent des formations spécifiques aux travaux en hauteur, aux interventions dans les espaces confinés et au montage d'échafaudages. Le centre comprend également une section consacrée à la formation professionnelle dans plusieurs métiers, notamment l'électricité industrielle, la mécanique diesel des engins lourds, les équipements fixes et la soudure. Du concassage au convoyage : les différentes étapes du traitement du minerai Autre étape importante de cette immersion : la découverte des installations de concassage et de traitement du minerai après son extraction. Mohamed Fodé Condé, superviseur concassage, a expliqué le fonctionnement des équipements chargés de réduire progressivement la dimension des blocs de minerai de fer. Le processus commence notamment au niveau du concasseur primaire, également appelé « sizer », dont le rôle est de réduire la taille granulométrique du minerai. À la sortie de cette première installation, le minerai est acheminé par un convoyeur, un tapis roulant industriel qui permet de le déplacer d'un point à un autre. Il passe ensuite par une deuxième zone de traitement équipée de concasseurs secondaires. Ces installations permettent de réduire davantage la dimension du minerai, jusqu'à 125 millimètres. Le traitement se poursuit à travers les concasseurs secondaires 1 et 2, avant que le minerai ne soit transporté par un autre convoyeur industriel de plus de deux kilomètres jusqu'à la tour de transfert, appelée « Transfer Tower ». Ces différentes opérations permettent de préparer le minerai en fonction des caractéristiques granulométriques attendues pour la suite de la chaîne de production. Chargement des wagons : dernière étape avant l'acheminement vers Morebaya La dernière phase de la visite a permis aux journalistes de découvrir les opérations de préparation et de chargement du minerai dans les trains. Sur ce volet, Georges Guilavogui, ingénieur des mines avec 18 ans d'expérience dans l'industrie minière et directeur adjoint du projet au sein de GPC, entreprise de droit guinéen, a expliqué le mécanisme mis en place pour alimenter les trains. Arrivé sur le projet en février 2025, il indique avoir été recruté pour coordonner les activités de GPC en vue du premier chargement des trains et accompagner Simfer dans les premières opérations d'exploitation de la mine. Selon ses explications, le processus consiste à acheminer le minerai depuis une zone de stockage appelée IOS vers le TLO, où s'effectuent les opérations de préparation et de chargement des wagons. Au niveau de l'IOS, des équipements appelés scalpeurs permettent de trier le minerai afin de récupérer les particules fines répondant aux spécifications recherchées. En complément, une partie du minerai extrait de la mine par Mota et stocké sur cette plateforme est acheminée vers des concasseurs mobiles pour être réduite à la granulométrie souhaitée. Les produits obtenus sont ensuite stockés avant leur transfert vers les aires de chargement. Au total, six aires sont aménagées pour ces opérations. Deux catégories de minerai y sont actuellement disponibles, selon les spécifications granulométriques demandées par le client : un premier produit de 125 millimètres et un second de moins de 40 millimètres. « Actuellement, nous chargeons les deux types de produits en fonction du besoin du client », a précisé Georges Guilavogui. Il a également indiqué que les trains utilisés pour le transport du minerai sont composés de 100 wagons, chacun disposant d'une capacité de chargement de 80 tonnes. Cette immersion de deux jours a ainsi permis aux journalistes guinéens de suivre, à travers les explications des responsables techniques, les différentes opérations qui structurent la chaîne de production du site minier exploité par Rio Tinto et Simfer. De la formation des travailleurs à la caractérisation géologique du gisement, en passant par le concassage, le convoyage et le chargement ferroviaire, les professionnels des médias ont pu appréhender les différentes étapes qui conduisent le minerai de son extraction jusqu'à son acheminement vers les installations portuaires de Morebaya, dans Forécariah. Sadjo Bah L’article Immersion à Simandou : de l'extraction du minerai au chargement des trains, des journalistes découvrent les coulisses des opérations menées par Rio Tinto Simfer est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Des missions gouvernementales dans trois wilayas du pays pour définir les projets prioritaires de la 2ème phase du programme d’urgence
items.description: Des délégations ministérielles mauritaniennes ont entamé une série de rencontres avec les citoyens dans les wilayas de Gorgol, du Brakna et du Guidimakha, afin de définir les projets prioritaires de la deuxième phase du programme d'urgence visant à généraliser l'accès aux services essentiels au développement local, des consultations qui porteront sur 11 wilayas de l'intérieur du pays. Le gouvernement a indiqué, lors d’un point presse, que la sélection des projets s’appuierait sur les besoins de la population, à l’instar de la première phase du programme, sans toutefois préciser la date de lancement de la deuxième phase ni le montant des financements qui lui seront alloués. Selon ce communiqué, des responsables administratifs, des élus ainsi que des représentants d’organisations de jeunesse et de femmes, de partis politiques et d’organisations de la société civile ont participé à ces rencontres. Le gouvernement a ajouté que les participants avaient salué les résultats obtenus au cours de la première phase et avaient exprimé leur espoir que la deuxième phase réponde aux besoins qui n’ont pas encore été couverts.

items.title: Communications Minister Sam George confirmed as chair of AU STC on Communication and ICT
items.description: Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George (MP), has been confirmed as Chair of the African Union Specialised Technical Committee on Communication and ICT (AU STC-ICT) at its 6th Ordinary Session in Libreville, Gabon. In his opening address to the ministerial session, the Minister described the chairmanship as a responsibility to the entire African Union, emphasising the need for stronger continental cooperation to accelerate Africa’s digital transformation. “I accept such responsibility not as a privilege for one country, but as a duty to our entire union,” he said. Addressing Africa’s digital priorities, Hon. George called for a decisive shift from policy development to implementation, noting that the continent already has key frameworks on digital transformation, artificial intelligence and data governance. “What we have too often lacked is the collective will to implement them at the pace that our people demand,” he stated. He highlighted connectivity, data governance, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence as critical areas requiring coordinated action, stressing that Africa must take a more active role in shaping the global digital economy. “When we negotiate alone, we are 55 separate markets, but when we negotiate together, we are a market of nearly 1.5 billion people,” he said, adding that Africa must be “at the table, not on the menu” in global conversations on artificial intelligence, data and digital trade. The Minister also underscored the importance of equipping Africa’s young population with the skills and opportunities to innovate, drawing attention to Ghana’s One Million Coders Programme as an example of what young people can achieve when given the right tools. Setting out his priorities for the chairmanship, Hon. George pledged to build consensus, strengthen cooperation and drive implementation across the continent. “Over the next two years, this committee must be measured not by the declarations that we adopt, but by the results that we deliver,” he said. He called on member states to take bold decisions towards a shared digital future in which Africa can operate as one digital market and speak with one digital voice. Ghana’s chairmanship comes at a critical time as African countries work to expand digital access, strengthen cybersecurity, advance responsible AI development and ensure that the continent’s digital resources and opportunities serve its people.

items.title: Patrick Stewart, best known for “Star Trek” and “X-Men,” dies at 86
items.description: Legendary actor Sir Patrick Stewart, best known for his work in the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises and his prolific award-winning stage career, has died at 86 years old, his spokesperson confirmed. Stewart died at home on Wednesday, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said in a statement. His death followed “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” Novak said. “He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” Novak said. Stewart began his acting career doing stage plays in the United Kingdom, joining the Royal Shakespeare Company in the 1960s. Stewart’s most recognizable role began in 1987, when he started playing Enterprise Captain Jean-Luc Picard on “Star Trek: The Next Generation.” The show ran for seven seasons and also spawned four “Star Trek” films featuring Stewart as Picard and the rest of the “Next Generation” cast. Stewart later reprised the role for Paramount+ series “Star Trek: Picard,” which ran for three seasons. Fellow “Star Trek” legend William Shatner posted : “Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor. From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work.” George Takei, who played Hikaru Sulu in the original “Star Trek” series, said on Threads that “Stewart took the starship Enterprise to places it had never gone before, and he inspired a whole next generation of star-gazers who looked longingly ahead to a brighter future for all humanity. Our hearts are heavy, indeed. Rest in the heavens, Captain.” Stewart also played “X-Men” leader Charles Xavier in over half a dozen films in the “X-Men” franchise. He reprised the role for the upcoming “Avengers: Doomsday,” which will be released in December 2026. Marvel Studios said on social media that it was “deeply saddened” by Stewart’s passing, calling him a “singular talent” who defined the character “for generations of fans.” “X-Men” co-star Hugh Jackman said in a social media post “We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days.” Stewart appeared in dozens of other film and television roles, including voice work on Seth MacFarlane’s animated shows “Family Guy” and “American Dad.” “Patrick was one of those icons who we somehow all took for granted would always be with us,” MacFarlane wrote on social media Thursday. “… He was that rare actor who could take any bit of dialogue and elevate it, making a good writer sound great, and a great writer sound masterful. He was also as humble as they come … We have lost a legendary actor today, and for many of us, a good friend. He will be deeply missed by the entire planet.” The bulk of Stewart’s work was on the stage: He was a frequent presence on Broadway and in London’s West End, where he played characters from Shakespearean villains to Charles Dickens’ Ebenezer Scrooge. He appeared with “X-Men” co-star Ian McKellen in “Waiting for Godot” in London in 2010, then again in New York City in 2013. He also performed his one-man version of “A Christmas Carol” frequently over the decades. Stewart appeared in over 60 Royal Shakespeare Company productions. The company named him an “Honorary Associate Artist” to celebrate his contributions to their work. He has also been awarded three Olivier Awards for his London stage performances and received one Tony nomination for his work on Broadway. Stewart was nominated for multiple Emmy, Golden Globe and SAG awards for his on-screen roles. He won a Grammy Award in 1995 for “Best Spoken Word Album for Children.” In 2001, Queen Elizabeth II appointed Stewart an Officer of the Order of the British Empire. In 2010, Stewart received a knighthood, again from Elizabeth II, for his services to drama. In 2023, Stewart published the memoir “Making It So.” The book landed him on the New York Times’ best-sellers list. He also recorded a companion audiobook. Stewart was actively working until 2026. In addition to his role in “Avengers: Doomsday,” he recorded an audiobook where he narrated and commented on all 154 of William Shakespeare’s sonnets. He also had a voice role in the animated comedy “The Sheep Detectives.” Stewart was married three times. He wed Sheila Falconer in 1966. The pair had two children — Daniel and Sophia — before divorcing in 1990. From 2000 to 2003, he was married to producer Wendy Neuss. In 2008, he began dating singer-songwriter Sunny Ozell. The two married in 2013 and were wed until his death. Novak said Ozell was at Stewart’s side when he died. Stewart was also “a fierce advocate for causes he strongly believed in,” his spokesperson said. Those causes included social justice, women’s rights, domestic abuse advocacy, veterans’ rights, the refugee crisis, animal rights and political reform. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace,” Novak said. “His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre. … He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role — in his art and life.”

items.title: Court remands four over Worawora disturbances
items.description: The Dambai Circuit Court has remanded four people to police custody over their alleged involvement in disturbances at Dwabrem-Worawora in the Oti Region. The accused are Kwame Aboagye Ahenkora, 55, Prince Asante, 27, Daniel Wiafe, 20, and Kwabena Nsimbo, 22. Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) John Nchor, Public Affairs Officer of the Oti Regional Police Command , said the accused persons would reappear before the Court on November 17, 2026. He said the alleged disturbances occurred at Dwabrem on October 24, 2026, amid tensions over the commencement of rites for the Akwantutenten Festival. DSP Nchor said the incident allegedly involved the burning of vehicle tyres and other acts of violence following claims that a High Court injunction had been secured to restrain the celebration. He said Police personnel deployed to the area extinguished the fire and restored order. DSP Nchor said the Oti Regional Security Council (REGSEC), at a meeting with representatives of the disputing families on October 26, directed the parties to seek redress through the courts and the Houses of Chiefs. He said the Council stressed that the chieftaincy dispute must be resolved through lawful means and directed that all persons arrested in connection with the disturbances be dealt with in accordance with the law. DSP Nchor said the Oti Regional Police Command had appealed to all parties to remain calm, exercise restraint and respect lawful processes to help maintain peace and security in Worawora.

items.title: Osimhen welcomes second child with Cameroonian-German girlfriend
items.description: Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen and his girlfriend, Stefanie Ladewig, have welcomed their second child, a baby girl named Liora Audrey. Galatasaray, the Turkish club where Osimhen plays, announced the arrival of the couple’s daughter in a social media post on Thursday. “Our Football A Team player Victor Osimhen and Stefanie have welcomed a baby girl into the world. “We congratulate the couple Victor and Stefanie; we wish their newborn baby Liora Audrey a long, healthy, and happy life!” the post read. The couple’s first daughter, Hailey, was born in October 2022. Ladewig, a Cameroonian-German fashion model and social media influencer, reportedly began dating Osimhen in 2019 when the Nigerian forward was playing for German Bundesliga side Wolfsburg. Earlier this month, reports emerged that Ladewig had been involved in a road accident while heavily pregnant. Turkish media reported that she escaped unhurt in the crash, which involved three vehicles. Meanwhile, Osimhen is expected to feature for Galatasaray in their league fixture against T. Konyaspor on Friday, having been included in the squad for the match. The 27-year-old forward was in impressive form on Monday, scoring twice to help Galatasaray defeat their fierce Istanbul rivals, Fenerbahce, in the city derby. Galatasaray currently lead the league standings after nine matches, while Osimhen has scored eight goals, placing him among the competition’s joint-top scorers. items.title: La diphtérie réapparaît, 25 cas suspects signalés dans plusieurs ville du Nord
items.description: La réapparition de la diphtérie au Maroc en 2026 suscite de nouvelles inquiétudes sanitaires, notamment dans la région de Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceïma, où plusieurs cas suspects et confirmés ont été signalés. Des données officielles fournissent des détails sur la répartition géographique des cas signalés. Alors que la diphtérie n’avait plus été signalée au Maroc depuis 1992, sa réapparition en 2026 soulève des inquiétudes sanitaires, notamment en raison de la baisse de la couverture vaccinale et du nombre d’enfants non vaccinés ou dont le calendrier vaccinal est incomplet. Cette maladie infectieuse, qui peut entraîner de graves complications et parfois le décès, rappelle l’importance de la vaccination et du renforcement de la surveillance épidémiologique. Face à cette situation, les autorités sanitaires poursuivent les efforts de dépistage et de prise en charge des personnes touchées afin de limiter la propagation de l’infection. Selon des données officielles, une attention particulière est donnée à la région du nord du Maroc où des cas ont été recensés dans plusieurs provinces. Pour rappel, en début de semaine, un cas d'infection et le décès d'un enfant originaire de Ksar El Kebir a suscité les inquiétudes des autorités sanitaires. A l'heure actuelle, la région du nord a enregistré 25 cas suspects répartis dans 7 provinces sur les 8 que compte la région. Ces cas ont été pris en charge conformément au protocole sanitaire en vigueur au niveau national, et 14 patients se sont rétablis, selon des données officielles. La province de Larache arrive en tête avec huit cas, dont deux ont été confirmés. Deux patients se sont rétablis après avoir suivi un traitement, tandis que quatre autres cas sont en cours de vérification à la suite des analyses de laboratoire nécessaires. Dans la province de Tétouan, cinq cas suspects ont été enregistrés dont deux confirmés, tandis qu’un autre est toujours en attente de confirmation. Les deux autres patients ont reçu un traitement et ont quitté l’hôpital. Au niveau de la préfecture de Tanger-Assilah, quatre cas suspects sont sous surveillance des autorités sanitaires. L’un des cas suspectés de porter la diphtérie est en attente des résultats des analyses de laboratoire, tandis que trois patients ont été pris en charge et ont pu être rétablis après avoir reçu les soins nécessaires. Le même nombre de cas a été recensé dans la préfecture de M’diq-Fnideq, dont un confirmé. Les trois autres patients ont reçu un traitement et ont quitté l’hôpital. Enfin, deux cas suspects ont été enregistrés aussi bien à Chefchaouen, Fahs-Anjra qu'à Ouezzane. Les personnes concernées ont reçu les soins nécessaires et ont quitté les établissements hospitaliers où elles avaient été admises. Ces nombreux cas détectés dans le nord du pays viennent après la réapparition fin septembre dernier de la diphtérie dans la région de Souss-Massa, soit dans le sud du pays. La région avait enregistré deux foyers familiaux, respectivement dans la préfecture d’Agadir Ida-Outanane et dans la province de Chtouka-Aït Baha. Ces foyers concernaient des enfants non vaccinés ou n’ayant pas reçu l’ensemble des doses prévues dans le calendrier vaccinal. Cette situation où 25 cas suspects dont 14 rétablis après avoir reçu un traitement témoigne de la rapidité de la propagation ainsi que de la prise en charge de cette maladie potentiellement mortelle. Pour éviter l'infection à la diphtérie, la vaccination constitue le principal moyen de prévention. Le Programme national de vaccination prévoit trois doses initiales à l’âge de deux, trois et quatre mois, suivies de doses de rappel à 18 mois et à cinq ans. Les doses manquantes peuvent également être rattrapées en fonction du statut vaccinal de chaque enfant. La lutte contre les cas suspects nécessite un diagnostic précoce, un isolement médical et l’administration d’un traitement adapté. Les personnes ayant été en contact avec les malades doivent être également identifiées et leur état de santé suivi, notamment au sein des familles et des établissements scolaires, afin de limiter les risques de transmission. items.title: CAN : Motsepe annonce une décision imminente sur le retour au rythme biennal
items.description: Moins d’un an après avoir annoncé le passage de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN) à une périodicité de quatre ans, Patrice Motsepe semble désormais se rapprocher d’un retour au format historique. Le président de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a indiqué, jeudi à Doha, qu’une décision serait annoncée prochainement, alors que les premières consultations font état d’un large soutien des fédérations à une CAN tous les deux ans. Le calendrier de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations pourrait connaître un nouveau changement de cap. Intervenant jeudi à Doha, au Qatar, dans le cadre de l’événement CNN Global Perspectives, Patrice Motsepe est revenu sur la périodicité de la principale compétition du football africain, au lendemain de la clôture d’une consultation menée auprès des 54 fédérations membres de la CAF. Le président de l’instance continentale a confirmé qu’une décision serait prise prochainement, évoquant un soutien important en faveur du maintien d’une CAN organisée tous les deux ans. « J’avais annoncé il y a quelques semaines, au Cap-Vert, que nous allions réexaminer cette question. Il y avait un large soutien en faveur d’un retour à une CAN tous les deux ans, ce que j’ai toujours soutenu », a déclaré Motsepe. Le dirigeant sud-africain a également indiqué avoir reçu de nombreux courriers des associations membres plaidant pour le maintien de cette périodicité. « Une décision sera prise et je suis convaincu que ce sera la bonne. Nous l’annoncerons très prochainement » , a-t-il ajouté. Les fédérations appelées à se prononcer Selon SABC Sport, le secrétaire général par intérim de la CAF, Samson Adamu, a adressé cette semaine une circulaire aux 54 fédérations membres afin de recueillir leur position sur deux options : une CAN tous les deux ans ou tous les quatre ans. La date limite fixée pour transmettre leurs réponses était le mercredi 28 octobre. Les premiers retours rapportés font apparaître une préférence marquée pour le maintien du rythme biennal, en vigueur depuis plusieurs décennies. Cette tendance pourrait conduire la CAF à revoir la réforme annoncée en décembre 2025, même si aucune décision officielle n’a encore été communiquée. Une réforme annoncée en décembre 2025 Le 20 décembre 2025, à la veille du lancement de la CAN au Maroc, Patrice Motsepe avait annoncé que la compétition passerait à une périodicité de quatre ans après les éditions de 2027 et 2028. Cette perspective marquait une rupture avec le format historique du tournoi, organisé tous les deux ans depuis sa création en 1957. L’annonce avait suscité des critiques parmi les observateurs du football africain, notamment sur ses conséquences sportives et économiques. La diminution de la fréquence de la CAN soulevait en particulier la question des revenus générés par la compétition, qui constitue une source importante de financement pour la CAF et ses autres compétitions. Pour accompagner cette réforme, l’instance avait annoncé la création d’une Ligue des nations africaine. Toutefois, cette nouvelle compétition pourrait nécessiter plusieurs années avant de produire des recettes comparables à celles de la CAN. Dès le début du mois d’octobre, la possibilité d’un abandon de la réforme avait commencé à être évoquée. Patrice Motsepe avait ensuite confirmé, lors d’une intervention au Cap-Vert, que la question ferait l’objet d’un nouvel examen. Le projet de passage à une CAN tous les quatre ans avait également rencontré l’opposition de plusieurs acteurs du football africain. Hervé Renard, sélectionneur de la Côte d’Ivoire, s’était notamment prononcé contre cette évolution. Le retour à une CAN tous les deux ans pourrait être entériné lors de l’Assemblée générale ordinaire de la CAF, prévue le 21 novembre à Abuja, au Nigeria. Cette échéance est désormais attendue pour connaître l’orientation définitive de l’instance sur le calendrier de la compétition. items.title: Dr. Bawumia confers with KAS Secretary-General; discusses Ghana’s future and NPP reorganisation
items.description: Former Vice President and New Patriotic Party (NPP) presidential candidate, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, has held high-level talks with the Secretary-General of the Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung (KAS), Dr. Mark Speich, in Accra on Thursday. KAS is one of Germany’s leading political foundations and is internationally affiliated with the NPP. Dr. Bawumia’s Accra engagement with them centred on developments in Ghana’s political landscape and efforts being made to reorganise the New Patriotic Party. Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia and the Secretary-General of the Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung (KAS), Dr. Mark Speich The NPP leader used the occasion to reiterate his resolve to rebuild the NPP, disclosing that over the last two years, deliberate steps have been taken to reinforce the party’s internal structures to make it more responsive to the concerns of ordinary Ghanaians. He further updated KAS on the progress of two flagship party projects – the Patriotic Institute and the Policy Unit. Describing both initiatives as “close to his heart,” Dr. Bawumia said they are designed to groom future political leadership, open up avenues for youth participation in public service, and guarantee that NPP policies are grounded in evidence, financially sound and practicable. He indicated that the ultimate objective is to transform the NPP into a “more inclusive, intellectually vibrant and policy-oriented party with the capacity to drive Ghana’s sustainable development.” The Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung, which is linked to Germany’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU), has for years worked closely with the NPP, supporting programmes in democratic governance, institutional strengthening and policy development. Thursday’s meeting is part of a broader round of consultations Dr. Bawumia is holding with international partners and local stakeholders as part of the NPP’s reorganisation drive ahead of the 2028 polls.

items.title: Hammouchi accorde une promotion exceptionnelle au policier blessé à Agadir
items.description: Le directeur général du pôle DGST-DGSN, Abdellatif Hammouchi, a décidé jeudi d’accorder une promotion exceptionnelle au policier grièvement blessé après avoir été volontairement percuté à plusieurs reprises par un automobiliste à Agadir. Le policier, qui occupait le grade de brigadier-chef au sein de la brigade mobile des motards relevant de la préfecture de police d’Agadir, a été promu au grade d’officier de paix, indique un communiqué de la Direction générale de la sûreté nationale (DGSN), notant que cette décision vise à reconnaître son sens du devoir et les sacrifices consentis dans l’exercice de ses missions. Selon les éléments rapportés, le fonctionnaire a été volontairement percuté à plusieurs reprises par un véhicule dont le conducteur avait refusé d’obtempérer à un ordre d’arrêt. Le conducteur avait auparavant forcé un barrage judiciaire installé à l’entrée de la ville d’Agadir. Le policier est intervenu pour tenter de l’intercepter, avant d’être grièvement blessé et transporté à l’hôpital pour recevoir les soins nécessaires. Prise en charge médicale et sociale Cette promotion exceptionnelle intervient en application de l’article 29 du statut particulier des fonctionnaires de la sûreté nationale, qui prévoit des mesures en faveur des policiers victimes de blessures ou exposés à des risques dans l’exercice de leurs fonctions. Dans ce même contexte, Abdellatif Hammouchi a chargé les services médicaux et sociaux de la DGSN d’apporter au fonctionnaire blessé le soutien matériel et moral nécessaire. L’ensemble des frais liés à son traitement et à son hospitalisation sera également pris en charge. À travers cette décision, la Direction générale de la sûreté nationale réaffirme l’attention portée à ses fonctionnaires victimes d’agressions dans l’exercice de leurs missions et entend reconnaître les sacrifices consentis par les éléments de police pour assurer la sécurité des citoyens. items.title: Ghana targets $1.2bn investment and 150,000 jobs under new textile policy
items.description: Ghana is targeting about $1.2 billion in investment and 150,000 direct and indirect jobs over the next decade under a new textile and garment policy approved by Cabinet. The policy, which is expected to be formally launched by the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, also seeks to expand the country’s textile and garment industry from an estimated $400 million to about $2 billion. It further aims to revive domestic cotton production across 50,000 hectares as part of efforts to strengthen local raw material supply and support the growth of the industry. The targets were announced by the Trade Ministry’s Director of Research, George Amoah, at the launch of the second phase of the International Labour Organization’s (ILO) Productivity Ecosystem for Decent Work programme. Mr Amoah described the textile and garment industry as a significant source of employment, with the potential to create decent jobs and help address unemployment. He cited estimates indicating that the global garment sector employs about 94 million people, with women accounting for between 60 and 80 per cent of the workforce. However, he said investment in factories and equipment alone would not be enough to achieve the sector’s growth ambitions. “We need a skilled workforce, efficient production systems, strong management, compliance with standards and workplaces where people can perform at their best,” he said. At the same event, ILO Programmes Manager Bismark Ghartey outlined some of the achievements of the first phase of the Productivity Ecosystem for Decent Work programme. He said the programme supported the development of Ghana’s first productivity statistics, providing a national evidence base for discussions on productivity, employment, wages and policy. Mr Ghartey also cited developments in the shea sector, where the programme supported the establishment of the Shea Employers Association and the Ghana Shea Workers Union. The two organisations subsequently signed what he described as the sector’s first collective bargaining agreement in 2026. He said the agreement provided a framework for employers and workers to address shared concerns through dialogue. ILO Global Programmes Manager for the Productivity Ecosystem for Decent Work, Stephan Ulrich, said the second phase would build on the initial programme by coordinating productivity improvements at the policy, labour and enterprise levels. He stressed the need for deliberate pathways to help workers transition into more decent employment, noting that economic growth does not automatically translate into job creation. The programme is funded by the Swiss government through the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs. Switzerland’s Deputy Head of Mission and Head of Cooperation to Ghana, Janine Walz, called for a coordinated approach to job creation, stressing that improvements in productivity and employment require collaboration across businesses and institutions. The Productivity Ecosystems for Decent Work programme adopts an integrated approach to improving productivity and working conditions at enterprise, sectoral and national levels. It seeks to address structural factors contributing to low productivity and high informality rather than focusing only on their effects. The proposed textile and garment policy is expected to form part of broader efforts to attract investment, strengthen local production and improve employment opportunities in the sector.

items.title: Google value plunges by $500bn as AI fears rattle Wall Street
items.description: Google parent Alphabet lost just over $500bn (£374bn) in value on Thursday after it rattled Wall Street with its last update of the year on its business operations. Google spooked investors so badly that its stock hit a six-month low, after it revealed its artificial intelligence (AI) summaries on search were affecting ad revenue. Microsoft and Amazon also updated investors this week, and joined Google in plans to keep spending astronomical sums of cash in an ongoing AI race. But investors appeared dismayed at the impacts these plans are having on the ability of each to keep growing their core lines of business. Google AI is eating its core business – search At first glance, the quarterly results of Alphabet, the parent company of Google, were not at all bad. Total revenue grew 25% compared to last year, hitting $127.6bn. It was buoyed by the ongoing success of Google Cloud, where revenue grew by 103% to almost $31bn. However, profits at the company fell by a considerable 25% during the quarter. And for the second time in its history as a public company, it showed negative free cash flow, this time in excess of $9bn. That’s almost twice the loss of cash Alphabet showed just three months ago. Cash flow represents the money a company retains after paying for operations and investments, meaning Alphabet is now spending more money than it is bringing in. That new level of spending is almost entirely dedicated to Google’s AI investments. By the end of Thursday, the company’s total stock market value had fallen to $3.46 trillion from $3.97 trillion the day before. Google’s omnipresent search engine now defaults to AI summaries of a person’s query, and that hit the number of advertisements it was able to sell during the quarter. The sale of ads that appear alongside Google Search results is the vast majority of Alphabet’s business. Tracy Woo, a principal analyst at Forrester, said Alphabet’s disappointing search business results “highlights the challenge of funding massive AI investments while maintaining the strength of established businesses.” Although Phillip Schindler, Google’s chief business officer, said on Wednesday that he felt “very good about our trajectory” with an AI-focused version of the search engine, the company’s stock fell by almost 13% on Thursday, its second lowest showing this year. Investors not buying Amazon’s trillion-dollar business hopes Amazon’s stock also took a hit on Thursday after it shared results that disappointed investors. Shares of the company fell 6% in after hours stock trading. Alongside quarterly sales growth of 11%, hitting $201bn, the company shared a staggering cash flow figure of negative $42bn. That number shows that Amazon is not only spending more money than it makes, but that spending has increased six-fold over the span of three months. Chief executive Andy Jassy claimed the business was spending in part because it had the chance at, not one, but two businesses that could end up bringing in $1 trillion for Amazon the future. Jassy did not specify what two Amazon businesses those may be. But during a call with financial analysts he repeatedly mentioned the financial opportunity presented by Amazon making and selling its own computer chips, as well as its AI developer platform Bedrock, which offers paying users access to most major AI models and tools. “One of the lessons we’ve learned over 20-plus years is that there is not one tool to rule the world,” Jassy said. “People always assume whatever is in the lead early on will be the only thing that people use – it’s never true.” As Jassy was asked several times to explain the company’s spending, he admitted it “would be more convenient” if it were spread over the next 25 years. “That’s not the world we live in,” he added. “We can fund this plan, and I think it will forever change the size, the revenue, the free cash flow of Amazon.” Microsoft begs the question of AI’s real value Wall Street reacted less enthusiastically to Microsoft’s update, with shares falling by less than 1% on Thursday. The company, which is also one of OpenAI’s largest investors, spent around $5bn less on investments dedicated to AI. It also revealed earlier this week plans to cut thousands of workers , which will further reduce the company’s costs. Meanwhile, its revenue grew 19% from a year earlier, hitting $92.3bn for the quarter. Its crucial cloud business grew by 30% to $63bn. Chief executive Satya Nadella said the use of Copilot, Microsoft’s AI chatbot and tool, has seen “automated tasks nearly double since July” as daily users grew by 500% from a year ago. Usually lower spending and growing sales earns a positive reaction from investors. But Woo said Wall Street is trying to look farther into the future when it comes to which businesses will truly make good on their big promises around AI. “Microsoft’s results reinforce that enterprise demand for AI remains strong, but they also highlight a much bigger question facing the technology industry, where AI value will ultimately be captured,” Woo said.

items.title: Sécurité : la police dément une infox sur un prétendu recensement à domicile
items.description: La direction générale de la Police nationale a publié un communiqué officiel, ce 29 octobre 2026, pour alerter les citoyens face à la propagation de fausses informations sur les réseaux sociaux. L'institution met en garde contre de supposés agents de police qui effectueraient du porte-à-porte pour un prétendu « recensement de la population » ou des contrôles d'identité en s'appuyant sur de faux documents aux couleurs du ministère de l'Intérieur. La police affirme qu’il s’agit «d'infox (fake news)», tout en précisant que ces pratiques n’émanent ni du ministère ni de l'institution policière, et appelle la population à faire preuve de la plus grande vigilance en n'accordant aucun crédit à ces publications. items.title: UPSA Graduates 1,314 Students at 18th Congregation
items.description: The University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), on Wednesday held the third session of its 18th Congregation at the Kofi Ohene Konadu Auditorium, where 1,314 students from the Faculty of Management Studies graduated. Various awards were presented to students who excelled. The cohort comprised 1,009 undergraduate degree recipients and 305 diploma recipients. They form part of the 5,120 students expected to graduate across the University’s 18th Congregation sessions. In his report, the Vice-Chancellor, Professor John Kwaku Mensah Mawutor, urged the new graduates to uphold integrity and accountability while pursuing continuous learning to remain relevant in a changing professional environment. “Let integrity and accountability guide you as you step into the next chapter of your lives,” he said. He encouraged the graduates to harness emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI), responsibly while exercising independent judgement. He further urged them to remain curious, adaptable and committed to developing their knowledge and skills, and to build professional reputations grounded in competence, integrity and service. The Special Guest of Honour, Managing Director of Appointed Time Limited, Jacqueline Afful, urged the graduates to pair desire with discipline, direction and character in order to succeed in the world of work. She said graduation marks the end of a long journey that began with excitement upon receiving admission letters, particularly for those who got their desired courses. According to her, one of the most powerful forces in human life is desire, and every graduate has a dream they desire to achieve, but the critical question is how many are willing to go through the process to achieve it. On corporate sustainability in Ghana, Mrs. Afful said one of the fears of most organisations is how to transcend generations, a challenge she linked to the attitude of young graduates towards hard work. Recounting an experience in her company, she said 10 National Service Personnel who served in 2025, when asked about their career aspirations and which department they would like to join if retained, all chose Human Resources, including those who studied Marketing. When asked why they were not interested in marketing, a field they studied and served in, she said they responded that marketers suffer too much because of constant pressure over targets during management and performance reviews. “At this time, we all want to do HR,” she quoted them as saying, adding that the company eventually had to let go of the graduates. Mrs. Afful said the incident illustrates a simple truth: “In this world, it is those who want to go the extra mile, those who want to do the hard work, who can achieve success. “She told the graduates that while they have earned their degrees and some have already started their national service or dream jobs, the degree may not necessarily be the path of their future growth. She noted that it is normal to change career paths, as long as one is still driven by desire, but cautioned that desire must have discipline and direction. She reminded them that the world is big enough for everyone and that UPSA has equipped them to either seek employment or come together to form their own organisations. She warned that there will be financial difficulties and stiff competition, but urged them to be determined to do more and go the extra mile. “Go out there and be champions of your profession,” she charged the graduates.

items.title: Omitted candidates: INEC upholds 41 of governorship petitions, rejects 28
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has upheld 41 of the 69 petitions filed against the final list of governorship candidates for the 2027 general election, while rejecting 28. Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC) of the commission, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday night. According to him, the petitions came from 12 political parties across 26 states. He said, “The complaints concerned the omission of certain political parties, the wrongful inclusion of candidates of political parties whose names were not contained in the membership registers submitted by their political parties, and instances of alleged multiple nominations.” Haruna said the commission examined the complaints against its records and the law. “Following a review of the complaints, relevant records and applicable legal provisions, the Commission found merit in some representations and approved the inclusion of affected candidates and their political parties, while complaints found to be without merit were declined. “In addition, some names that were wrongfully published in the final list were removed after verifying that their names were not on the register. “The Commission also approved the removal of candidates whose nominations were found to be inconsistent with the applicable legal requirements,” the statement said. Although INEC did not name any candidate or state, a source had earlier revealed that the commission’s meeting on Thursday to review complaints from parties and candidates left out of the lists had cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections, subject to the outcome of pending court cases. The source also said the petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list, did not succeed. “Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said when asked about the PDP governorship candidate in Gombe State. “He did not succeed,” the source said when asked about Adebutu. On the State Houses of Assembly, the commission said the decisions affecting candidates sponsored by political parties “were informed by specific complaints received and determined in accordance with the law and the Commission’s established criteria.” For those elections, INEC received 61 petitions from 11 political parties across 11 states. Twenty-five succeeded, while 36 failed. The commission said the affected candidates, political parties and states “will be reflected in the updated list on the Commission’s website.” “Once again, the Commission assures the public of its commitment to transparency and the credibility of the electoral process,” the statement said. items.title: After Crash, Spain Asks if Its Train System Is Too Old and Prone to Human Error
Mbappé, Mao, and La Liga
items.description: Click to expand Image An advertisement featuring French soccer star Kylian Mbappé in Shanghai, China, June 30, 2026. © 2026 Chinatopix via AP Photo This week a Chinese sports forum unearthed an April 2026 interview with Real Madrid football star Kylian Mbappé jokingly likening himself to a “Chinese dictator” (dictateur chinois). While Mbappé, known for dictating terms on the pitch, did not name names, the broadcaster added art showing him as Chinese Communist Party founder Mao Zedong. Beijing’s reaction was swift. China’s Foreign Ministry claimed the words “hurt the feelings of the Chinese people.” Chinese state broadcaster CCTV blacked out all Spanish football league La Liga matches. The Chinese Communist Party under Xi Jinping has low tolerance for anything that could be interpreted as an affront to China, even a comment about Mao made in jest. Javier Tebas, the Spanish football league’s president, issued an apology praising La Liga’s ties with China’s “government departments.” Mao launched China’s Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution, disasters that caused massive loss of lives and suffering. In his 2008 book Tombstone: The Untold Story of Mao's Great Famine, journalist Yang Jisheng estimates that at least 36 million people starved to death or died from related abuse during the country’s famine from 1958 to 1961. There were periods when people in China could discuss aspects of these horrors. But, currently, under Xi’s ever-tightening grip, such questions won’t be tolerated. While Mbappé, who swiftly apologized, might lose Chinese sponsors, it’s China’s people who pay the greatest price. In 2021, the Chinese government passed a law punishing those who slander “heroes and martyrs” with up to three years in prison. The authorities later fined a comedian’s company 14.7 million yuan (about US$2.1 million) after he made a joke about the People’s Liberation Army. The authorities also recently sentenced artist Gao Zhen to three years in prison under the same law for his provocative Mao sculptures; in one, he depicted Mao kneeling and apologizing to his victims. Beijing’s response to Mbappé’s offhand remark is a reminder that, when it comes to controlling thought and speech, the Chinese Communist Party will always play to win.

items.title: Le FC Barcelone s’intéresse à Yassir Zabiri
items.description: Auteur d’un début de saison remarquable avec le Racing Santander, Yassir Zabiri attirerait l’attention du FC Barcelone. À 21 ans, l’attaquant marocain, prêté par le Stade Rennais jusqu’en juin 2027, affiche huit buts en dix matchs de Liga et voit sa valeur marchande grimper. Un intérêt qui pourrait ouvrir la voie à un nouveau tournant dans sa jeune carrière. Yassir Zabiri continue de faire parler de lui en Espagne. L’attaquant marocain du Racing Santander s’est imposé comme l’une des révélations offensives du début de saison en Liga, au point d’attirer, selon le média espagnol Fichajes, l’attention du FC Barcelone et de son directeur sportif, Deco. À 21 ans, le joueur affiche des statistiques particulièrement convaincantes avec huit buts inscrits en dix rencontres de championnat. Une efficacité qui le place parmi les attaquants les plus en vue du moment et renforce son attractivité sur le marché des transferts. Prêté par le Stade Rennais jusqu’au 30 juin 2027, Zabiri a su gagner progressivement sa place au sein de l’effectif cantabre. Initialement remplaçant d’Asier Villalibre, il aurait convaincu son entraîneur, José Alberto López, grâce à ses performances et à sa capacité à faire la différence dans les moments décisifs. Le dernier but de Zabiri face à l’Espanyol, lors d’une victoire 2-1 du Racing, illustre son influence grandissante. Son but inscrit en fin de rencontre a permis à son équipe de repartir avec trois points précieux après plusieurs journées sans victoire. L’attaquant marocain s’était également distingué lors du déplacement du Racing au Spotify Camp Nou, malgré la défaite de son équipe face au FC Barcelone sur le score de 7-2. Il avait alors trouvé le chemin des filets dans un stade qu’il rêvait de découvrir, lui qui suit le club catalan depuis son enfance. Cette performance renforce le récit d’un joueur dont la progression est étroitement liée à ses ambitions personnelles, mais aussi à son efficacité devant le but. Le Barça face à un dossier complexe L’intérêt prêté au FC Barcelone comporte toutefois plusieurs obstacles. Arrivé au Stade Rennais en provenance de Famalicão pour un montant estimé à 10 millions d’euros, Zabiri est actuellement prêté au Racing Santander sans option d’achat, selon les informations rapportées par Fichajes. Son contrat avec le club breton court jusqu’en 2029, tandis que sa clause libératoire dépasserait les 20 millions d’euros. Le Stade Rennais conserve donc le contrôle de son avenir et ne pourrait pas récupérer le joueur avant la fin de son prêt dans les conditions évoquées par le média espagnol. La valorisation de l’attaquant aurait déjà atteint environ 20 millions d’euros, portée par ses performances en Liga. Si cette dynamique se confirme, le club rennais pourrait se retrouver en position de force lors des prochaines discussions sur son avenir. items.title: Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 to reach League Cup quarter-finals
items.description: Everton swept into the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win against Newcastle on Thursday as they booked a clash against giant-killers Fleetwood. David Moyes’s side took the lead through James Garner’s first-half goal at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. Hayden Hackney doubled the lead with his first goal since his close-season move from Middlesbrough. Everton striker Thierno Barry netted in the second half and Dan Burn’s reply for Newcastle came far too late to stop the Toffees ending their three-match winless run. Chasing their first League Cup final appearance in 43 years, Everton will travel to fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in the week commencing December 14. The ‘Cod Army’ caused one of the biggest shocks in League Cup history on Tuesday when they beat Premier League champions Arsenal in a penalty shoot-out after a 1-1 draw at Highbury. Everton have never won the League Cup, losing their two final appearances in 1977 and 1984. Everton fans do not need reminding that it is 31 years since the club won the FA Cup in their most recent trophy triumph. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a noted Everton fan, is old enough to remember that success and he was cheering from the stands as Moyes’s men made light work of their last-16 tie. Newcastle will have the chance for revenge when the sides meet again in the Premier League at St James’ Park on Monday. Everton dropped a pre-match bombshell, saying Jack Grealish was unavailable for selection “due to a breach of club discipline”. Grealish, beset by criticism of his behaviour off the pitch, was reported to have taken an unauthorised absence from training. But the on-loan Manchester City winger’s absence was no problem for his team-mates. – Everton hit their stride – Newcastle tested Jordan Pickford early on when Joe Willock’s low drive was palmed away by the Everton goalkeeper, who repelled Fabian Schar’s long-range strike moments later. Garner steadied Everton’s nerves with a clinical opener in the 34th minute. Hackney teed up Garner just inside the area and the midfielder stretched to guide a fine finish into the far corner for his first goal since January. Everton had hit their stride and Hackney struck on the stroke of half-time. At the climax of a blistering Everton counter-attack, Barry hooked a cross into the six-yard box and Hackney timed his run perfectly to volley past Lukas Hornicek. Frustrated Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Joelinton, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa at the interval. Wissa had an immediate chance after sprinting onto Willock’s pass, but he misjudged the high bounce and ended up heading straight at Pickford. It was a costly miss as Barry put the result beyond doubt in the 69th minute. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall provided the cross and Barry lashed home from close range for his seventh goal this season. Burn scored with a header from Willock’s 88th-minute cross, sparking a brawl between several players. But Newcastle’s brief show of defiance was too little, too late as Everton moved a step closer to Wembley. items.title: 2027: Utomi, Ohaa, Yesufu urge Nigerians to mobilise support for Obi
items.description: Chieftains of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) have urged Nigerians to mobilise grassroots support for the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, come 2027. The party chieftains, including a political economist, Prof Pat Utomi, Enugu State NDC governorship candidate, Chief Chinyeaka Ohaa and human rights activist, Aisha Yesufu, made the call on Thursday during the Obi-Kwankwaso Town Hall Meeting held in Enugu. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Obi, his running mate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, and other NDC stakeholders attended the meeting, which attracted a large crowd of supporters. Addressing the crowd, Utomi expressed confidence that the Obi-Kwankwaso presidential ticket would provide the leadership needed to address Nigeria’s economic, political and security challenges. He lamented that Nigeria’s potential to become one of the greatest countries in the world had been undermined by corruption, criminality and disunity. According to him, the time has come for Nigerians to unite and work towards achieving meaningful political change. “We have done our research, and I know that a combination of Peter Gregory Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso will deliver Nigeria,” he said. Utomi urged Nigerians to turn out massively during the elections, vote for their preferred candidates and defend their votes through lawful means. In his remarks, Ohaa, the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, described the Obi-Kwankwaso political alliance as a historic opportunity to strengthen national unity and promote inclusive governance. He said the partnership represented the possibility of building political bridges across Nigeria’s geopolitical zones. According to him, the alliance is reminiscent of the historic political understanding between the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe and Sir Ahmadu Bello during Nigeria’s early political development. “My message today is simple: we must seize this opportunity and work with our brothers and sisters across the South-South, South-West, North-East, North-West and North-Central to secure an NDC president in 2027,” he said. Ohaa explained that the campaign was not merely about producing a president of Igbo extraction but about establishing a government committed to justice, accountability, security and prosperity for all Nigerians. He expressed confidence that NDC candidates in Enugu State were prepared to earn the trust of voters and secure victory in the elections. Yesufu, a human rights activist, urged Nigerians to take ownership of the 2027 elections by mobilising voters and actively participating in the democratic process. She said the election was not merely about Obi’s presidential ambition but about the collective responsibility of Nigerians to rescue the country from its numerous challenges. According to her, the election is not about Obi but about every one of us, as the mistake we made in 1999 must be corrected. “The class of 1999 has destroyed this country. The class of 2027 must fix this country. “We must take this election as our own election. Mr Peter Obi and his running mate have one business, and that is to be on the ballot paper.You and I must do the remaining work to ensure victory,” she said. Yesufu challenged every supporter to mobilise at least 20 eligible voters for Obi, stressing that political change required collective action rather than depending solely on candidates. The activist also urged Nigerians to demonstrate courage and determination in protecting their votes during the elections, saying that Nigerians must reject political intimidation and insist on credible elections that reflect the will of the people. Earlier, the NDC Chairman in Enugu State, Mr Ibuchukwu Obetta, welcomed Obi, Kwankwaso and other party leaders to the state, describing their visit as a significant moment in the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections. Obetta said the visit had renewed the confidence of party members and strengthened their determination to work for a Nigeria founded on integrity, accountability, competence, justice and inclusive development. (NAN) The post 2027: Utomi, Ohaa, Yesufu urge Nigerians to mobilise support for Obi appeared first on Vanguard News .
