items.title: Ten missing manhood cases false; Police vehicle vandalised at Breman
items.description: The Asankragwa Divisional Police Command has dismissed 10 reported cases of alleged missing manhood in its operational area as false, following medical examinations that confirmed the complainants’ genitalia were intact and medically normal. The Divisional Police Commander, Chief Superintendent (C/Supt) Vitus Napen, made the disclosure at a press briefing in Asankragwa. The briefing was attended by the District Police Commander, Superintendent James Ankan, and the Divisional Crime Officer, Mr John Kwakye. C/Supt Napen said the Division recorded the first case at Wassa Dunkwa on October 17, 2026, and has since recorded 10 similar cases. He said Wassa Dunkwa recorded six cases, Asankragwa two cases, Aboi Nkwanta one case and Breman one case. According to him, the complainants alleged that their genitalia had disappeared after coming into physical contact with other persons. C/Supt Napen said all complainants were referred for medical examination, which established that their genitalia were intact and medically normal. He added that preliminary investigations suggested that panic, anxiety and misinformation had contributed to the spread of the allegations. The Divisional Commander cautioned the public against raising false alarms over alleged missing genitalia, warning that such actions could attract legal consequences. He said persons found culpable could be prosecuted for offences related to the publication of false news and deceiving a public officer. Touching on an incident at Breman, C/Supt Napen said a mob attacked and vandalised a police patrol vehicle when officers arrived to rescue a suspect accused of causing the disappearance of a man’s genitalia. He said the mob smashed the rear windscreen of the vehicle in an attempt to lynch the suspect. C/Supt Napen condemned the incident, describing it as criminal, and warned that anyone who attacked security personnel or destroyed state property would be arrested and prosecuted. He urged the public to desist from taking the law into their own hands and to allow the Police to investigate such allegations. The Divisional Commander appealed to chiefs, opinion leaders and assembly members in the Wassa Amenfi West Municipality to intensify public education and encourage residents to report suspected criminal activities to the Police. He said no arrests had been made in connection with the vandalism as of the time of the briefing, adding that investigations were ongoing.

items.title: Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of trying to ‘delegitimise’ election
items.description: The main Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot and Arab-led party leaders have denounced Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for alleging foreign interference following the election which saw his coalition lose its majority. Netanyahu’s Likud accused Israel’s Arab-led parties of “stealing” the election. Home security agency Shin Bet is investigating whether they received illegal funding from Qatar and Turkey. Qatar’s foreign ministry denied the “ridiculous and dangerous” allegations and accused Israeli politicians of conducting a disinformation campaign against Doha. Final results confirmed that neither Netanyahu’s bloc nor the Jewish opposition had won a majority in parliament. The two Arab party lists – The Joint List and the Ra’am – defied expectations to win a record 19 seats in the 120-seat Knesset following a surge in turnout among Arab voters. That positions them as potential kingmakers, with Netanyahu’s bloc winning 53 seats and his rival Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc securing 48. On Thursday Likud alleged that voters had been “bribed” to vote for Arab parties, after the head of the Central Elections Committee (CEC) asked the Shin Bet security service to investigate “serious suspicions” of foreign interference. Both Arab parties strongly rejected the claim, with the Arab-majority Joint List alliance saying it was baseless. The row is being seen by Netanyahu’s critics as an attempt to delegitimise the Arab parties, thereby making it politically impossible for Eisenkot to join forces with them – which is currently his bloc’s only route to power. Arab-led parties including the Joint List headed by Yousef Jabareen (C) won a record 19 seats and could play a kingmaker role Israeli media reported that the CEC had been presented with a claim that Qatar had provided funding aimed at increasing voter turnout in Arab communities. Qatar’s Foreign Ministry “categorically” denied the claims. Netanyahu and his Likud Party framed the allegations as a “political earthquake” and an “an attack on democracy”, aimed at removing their right-wing government. But the Shin Bet later clarified that their investigation did not implicate an entire community who had voted legally, while acting CEC Director General Dean Livne said there was “no basis for allegations of systematic violations of election integrity.” Eisenkot, who was briefed on the investigation, said “it is too early to determine what happened, or if anything happened at all,” and accused Netanyahu of running “an orchestrated and organized campaign to delegitimize the election results”. Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh, who is part of the Joint List, dismissed the allegation, saying: “The losing side is constructing a racist blood libel and calling on the security agencies to use force in order to overturn the election results.” Netanyahu’s attacks on Arab voters and parties have been ongoing for days. He spent much of election day posting on social media that high Arab turnout is an “emergency” and a “matter of life or death” for the Israeli right. He also shared AI-generated images of Arab voters at polling stations, in an attempt to encourage right-wingers to get out and vote. Arab Israelis, many of whom refer to themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel, make up about one fifth of the country. For years, many boycotted Israeli elections, saying voting would legitimise a system that they say treats them as second-class citizens. But their turnout on Tuesday was inspired by a desire to oust the most right-wing governing coalition in Israel’s history, led by Netanyahu. The final results offer only three plausible options for a government to be formed: a national unity government involving Netanyahu and Eisenkot, a right-wing coalition involving Netanyahu and defectors from Eisenkot’s bloc, or an Eisenkot-led government supported by the Arab parties. Eisenkot and every member of his bloc bar one has previously refused to enter government with Arab parties, but speculation has swirled in recent days that an agreement could yet be reached. A snap poll conducted by Hebrew University showed that the most popular option for voters from every party in the opposition bloc was for Eisenkot to form a minority government with Ra’am, and supported from outside by the Joint List.

items.title: I’ll work closely with Kwankwaso if elected, Obi reassures
items.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has reiterated willingness to work closely with his vice-presidential candidate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, to move the country forward. Obi gave the assurance on Thursday during a town hall meeting in Enugu, where he engaged supporters and stakeholders on the country’s challenges and his vision for national development. The former Anambra State governor said they would work together to tackle insecurity and restore safety across Nigeria if elected president in 2027. He said that securing lives and property would be a priority of his administration, promising to confront the security challenges threatening communities and livelihoods across the country. The presidential candidate regretted that the current administration had failed to protect the lives and property of Nigerians, which he maintained was the primary responsibility. Obi assured voters in the South East to vote for him because of his competence and ability to tackle challenges facing the nation. He challenged other presidential candidates to meet and discuss their plans, and warned the people not to be deceived by rhetoric and propaganda. On education, Obi said he would declare a state of emergency on education to enable his administration to tackle the issue of out-of-school children head-on, hinting that Nigerian children deserved quality education. In his remarks, the vice-presidential candidate of NDC, Kwankwaso, advised that nobody should be deceived by ethnicity, saying, “It’s obvious that Nigerians are going through numerous difficulties”. Kwankwaso lamented that people were facing challenges like insecurity, unemployment, poverty, hunger and so many other challenges. He explained that the only solution to achieve a new Nigeria was unity, diligence, perseverance and willingness. He urged Nigerians to come out en masse to cast, protect and follow up on their votes until results were announced, noting that it was not a one-man show but a collective responsibility. Also, Sen Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly, described Obi and his running mate, Kwankwaso, as the “best presidential ticket” to lead Nigeria. Umeh expressed confidence that the South-East would rally behind Obi in the 2027 presidential election, urging the people to remain resolute and resist attempts to intimidate or discourage them from pursuing their political choice. He also commended the resilience of supporters who, according to him, ensured that the meeting held despite reported attempts to frustrate the gathering. The senator further praised Kwankwaso for his efforts to build support in Northern Nigeria, expressing optimism that the Obi-led ticket could attract votes across the country. Umeh urged the people of the South-East to use their votes to make a strong political statement in 2027, declaring his support for Obi’s presidential ambition and calling on the region to unite behind the project. items.title: George Michael’s Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row
items.description: The guitar George Michael performed with in his 1987 Faith music video has sold for £180,000 at auction, after a row over the sale of memorabilia related to the singer. The guitar was one of more than 30 items auctioned by Sworders from the collection of Siobhan Bailey, Michael’s long-time personal assistant. The sale fetched a total of £238,000 excluding buyers’ premium. Bailey died in 2014 and the items were sold by her estranged husband Ian Belcher, who inherited them after her death. Gerard Bailey, Siobhan’s brother, told the BBC she “would be horrified at the prospect of the auction being held in her name and that her personal, cherished possessions are being sold off to the highest bidder”. Belcher declined to comment. Sworders chairman Guy Schooling said Belcher had been “nothing but delightful” during their interactions over the past two-and-a-half years. “There are two ways of looking at this – it can be cashing in, or it can be a bit of a memorial and a tribute to Siobhan, and that’s the way we’ve looked at it,” he told BBC News. The auction house billed the 32 lots, including signed photographs, invitations to events and presentation CDs and discs,as a “remarkable group of memorabilia from the collection of Siobhan Bailey, George Michael’s long-time personal assistant and trusted confidante”. ‘Dishonourable and shameful’ Siobhan was in the process of divorcing Belcher when she died, but was legally still married to him. She did not leave a will. Her brother claimed she had started to draw up a will shortly before she died, which would have left the items to her nieces and nephews, but it was not registered. There is no suggestion that Belcher did not have the right to sell the items, because her estate legally passed to him when she died. Bailey said if his sister had lived a few weeks longer, the items would not have passed to Belcher because he would not have been considered her next of kin. In a letter to the auction house seen by the BBC, Bailey said the rest of the family considered the auction a “breach of [Siobhan’s] privacy”, adding that the use of her name was “disingenuous” and “wholly unethical”. He told the auction house that Belcher’s “misuse of my sister’s name” was “frankly dishonourable”, and profiteering from the items was “egregiously shameful”. Bailey asked that the auction should not go ahead, or be in Belcher’s name rather than Siobhan’s. The memorabilia on sale includes signed photographs of Wham! and George Michael on stage Siobhan Bailey began working as Michael’s personal assistant in 1984, joining him in the year Wham! had their first number-one hit with Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go. She remained his PA for 20 years, and her brother told BBC News she avoided the limelight and guarded the pop star’s privacy, despite the attention of tabloid journalists hoping for stories. “I think she was one of the few people George trusted and whose opinion he valued,” Bailey said. “She was always honest and straight with him. I guess that’s why she stayed working for him for so long through the very, very good and not so good times.” The guitar was “a gift” to his sister because the singer “thought so much of her”, he said. The instrument had a key role to play in Michael’s reinvention from teen pop idol to serious solo artist. In the 1987 video for Faith, Michael – in ripped blue Levi’s jeans, white T-shirt and black leather biker jacket – strummed the vintage acoustic guitar that he reportedly picked up in a shop in Los Angeles shortly beforehand. Guitarist magazine recently billed it as “arguably the most famous Gretsch Synchromatic in the world”. The auction’s biggest sales £180,000 – The Rockabilly Rebel guitar from the Faith video, with original hardshell case and leather guitar strap £7,000 – A Queen Five Live EP sleeve signed by Brian May, John Deacon, Roger Taylor, George Michael and Lisa Stansfield £5,000 – A Faith Tour ringbound itinerary from George Michael’s 1988 world tour £4,800 – A presentation CD of George Michael’s Older £4,500 – A gold disc of Wham!’s Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go £4,200 – A gold disc of George Michael’s I Want Your Sex Other items on sale included a note written “with love and admiration” from Michael and Andrew Ridgeley, an official Wham! photograph signed “To Siobhan (Special…)”, and an invitation to Ridgeley’s 21st birthday party. “I know she was proud of the various personalised gold and platinum discs she got, though she was very modest about it all,” Bailey said. Speaking before Thursday’s auction, he said “she would never have consented” to it, adding that the sale “breaks my heart”. “I think she’d be devastated that something as personal as her Filofax [tour itinerary] and notes from George are up for grabs. It’s just so tawdry and contrary to how she was,” he said. Siobhan died suddenly and unexpectedly of natural causes at the age of 56. According to her brother, she wanted the possessions to “have remained with her family and we would never have sold”. He accused Belcher of deciding “12 years after my sister’s death to cash in”. Bailey acknowledged that Belcher had a legal right to sell the items but called it “disingenuous” that the sale was being promoted in her name. George Michael grew up in Hertfordshire and shot to fame alongside Ridgeley in pop duo Wham! He went on to enjoy solo success with hits such as Faith, Careless Whisper, Father Figure, Outside and Fastlove. He died in 2016.

items.title: 47 university students attend first Unmute Yo’Self public speaking event in Accra
items.description: Forty-seven university students have participated in the first edition of Unmute Yo’Self, a free public speaking and confidence-building event aimed at helping young people communicate their ideas more effectively. The event was held on Friday, October 23, 2026, at the Accra AI Community Center in Ridge, Accra. Organised by the Sincerely Accra Podcast in collaboration with The Gold Coast Report (GCR), the programme was sponsored by Malta Guinness and Ashesi University. Participants included students from first year through to their final year. The initiative was designed to address the challenges young people face in expressing themselves confidently in classrooms, job interviews and professional settings. Organisers said the programme provides a supportive space for students to practise communication skills and develop the confidence to share their ideas. Co-creators of the Sincerely Accra Podcast, Joseph Nti and Kwame Asante Ofori, led sessions on public speaking and the responsible use of social media. Mr Nti, the podcast’s host, and Mr Ofori, its producer, guided participants on managing nervousness and structuring presentations around a clear opening, central message, supporting example, and conclusion. Guest speaker Nadia Daniel-Wilson addressed the topic “Using AI Without Surrendering Your Creativity,” encouraging students to use artificial intelligence tools to support their work without losing their individual voice and judgement. A panel of creative entrepreneurs also shared their experiences of building careers in the creative industry and turning their skills into income. The panel featured Shaunn Armah, a founder, creator and storyteller; Kabiru Seidu, co-founder and Director of Design and Strategy at The Big Fat African Development; and Seli Dzogbenuku, a writer, creative entrepreneur and podcast host. The discussions focused on their journeys into content creation, the opportunities available in the creative sector and the practical steps involved

items.title: Coupe des acteurs de la lutte contre la cybercriminalité : La Police nationale sacrée championne pour la deuxième fois consécutive
items.description: L’équipe de la Police nationale a remporté, le 29 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la finale de la deuxième édition du tournoi de maracana des acteurs de la lutte contre la cybercriminalité. Après un match nul (0-0) au terme du temps réglementaire, elle s’est imposée face à l’équipe de la Gendarmerie nationale à l’issue de la séance des tirs au but, remportée 2-1. La compétition, qui a réuni dix équipes, s’est achevée par cette rencontre intense, équilibrée et chargée de symboles. Aucune des deux formations n’a pu marquer pendant le temps réglementaire, et la séance de tirs au but a finalement départagé les équipes. Les joueurs de la Police nationale conservent ainsi le trophée, remporté pour la deuxième fois consécutive. Le vainqueur a reçu en plus des médailles d’or, un lot de maillots, des ballons et une somme de 500 000 francs CFA. L’international burkinabè Babayouré, désigné meilleur buteur de la compétition, s’est dit très satisfait de la performance collective. « Il n’y a pas de secret. Notre succès repose avant tout sur la solidarité et le fait de jouer en équipe », a-t-il déclaré. L’international burkinabè Babayouré, désigné meilleur buteur de la compétition -©Faso7 L’équipe de la Gendarmerie nationale, classée deuxième, a obtenu 300 000 francs CFA, des médailles d’argent, des maillots et des ballons. L’équipe de Wave Burkina, troisième, repart avec 150 000 francs CFA, des maillots et des ballons. Au-delà de l’enjeu sportif, cette finale a constitué un cadre de rassemblement et de promotion des valeurs de fraternité. Le Commandant Ahmed Ouédraogo, secrétaire général du ministère de la Sécurité, a souligné que cette rencontre a permis de célébrer le talent et le fair-play. Il a félicité les deux équipes finalistes pour leur parcours méritant. « Toutes nos félicitations à tous les acteurs qui ont participé à cette compétition, et félicitations aux équipes », a-t-il déclaré. À noter que ce tournoi est initié par la Brigade centrale de lutte contre la cybercriminalité (BCLCC), dans le cadre de la Semaine nationale de lutte contre la cybercriminalité (SNLC) . items.title: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17bn deal it says will expand customer options
items.description: DoorDash will acquire grocery delivery firm Instacart in a $17bn (£12.8bn) deal, creating a behemoth that will bring more meals, quick-need purchases and big weekly shops directly to customers. DoorDash said the deal, expected to be final in about a year, will expand customer options and let more sellers use the companies’ services. Instacart shoppers will be able to buy from 150,000 stores, up from 100,000, while DoorDash will expand beyond restaurants into retail, the firms said. “Together, we can accelerate innovation across the grocery industry and make online grocery more seamless and affordable for the millions of households we serve,” Instacart’s chief executive said. “Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more,” CEO Chris Rogers also said. For DoorDash, the acquisition will allow it to use Instacart’s grocery selection and substitution expertise, the company’s co-founder and chief executive, Tony Xu, said. “Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online. Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts,” Xu said. He added that “Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day”. The deal, expected to be done by the end of 2027 or first six months of 2028, is DoorDash’s biggest acquisition to date, and could help it take on delivery giants like Amazon. Morningstar analyst Martin Szumski told Reuters that the growth area in food delivery was shifting. “Restaurant delivery is maturing, and growth now lies in more frequent, higher-value orders: weekly grocery shops, convenience items, and retail,” he said. In the agreement, DoorDash will acquire Instacart for a value of $65 a share, which would be a 26% premium on the closing price of Instacart stock on 22 October – the price before news of the potential merger first emerged. The deal will be at least 75% cash, DoorDash said. DoorDash plans to keep Instacart’s brand, app, and technology products. The delivery services will keep operating as independent companies until the deal is concluded. The merger may raise antitrust issues with government regulators, Reuters also reported. New York City’s commission on consumer and worker protections, which last month reached a $131.5m settlement with DoorDash over allegations of underpaying workers, said in a statement: “This proposed merger continues a troubling trend of mega-corporations consolidating.” “Whether or not this merger proceeds, we will fully enforce delivery workers’ rights,” it added.

items.title: Inter, AC Milan unveil new stadium plans to replace San Siro
items.description: Inter and AC Milan unveiled their new “Generali Stadium” Thursday, which will replace the iconic San Siro stadium from the 2031/32 season. It will be shaped “low in the body, and it rises up at either end” behind the goals, architect Norman Foster said during a press conference in Milan. The design aims to bring spectators as close to the pitch as possible, with the stands behind the goals set at a steep 37-degree incline, said David Manica, a stadium specialist who collaborated with Foster on the project. “The most important thing that we realised when we designed this project is that the San Siro is a feeling,” he said. “It’s more than a building, it’s a feeling, and everything that we needed to do here was to carry it into the (new) building”. Manica said the design team “started with proximity”. “We brought all the seats as close as possible to the field. They could not be any closer, it’ll actually feel as though you’re sitting on the grass,” he said. They also paid great attention to acoustics: the roof covers the stands, leaving only the pitch exposed, and is designed to “amplify the roar” of the fans, Manica said. “This building is steeper than many other new buildings are built today, and that’s intentional, because it allows us to bring those seats up and over the field as much as possible, and create that sense of intimacy and atmosphere,” he said. The stadium, sponsored by the Italian insurance giant Generali, will also be capable of hosting American football games, rugby matches and concerts. “I want the crowd to come to the new stadium and to feel that excitement that they felt before, and to feel the building, living and breathing with them as it does currently,” Manica said. AC Milan and Inter paid 197 million euros ($219 million) to acquire the current stadium and its adjacent parking areas, where they intend to build their new, shared home. The project for the new San Siro — which will have a capacity of 71,500 seats, compared to the current 75,000 — will cost the two clubs 1.2 billion euros. Construction is set to begin in 2028. Foster and Manica previously worked together on London’s Wembley Stadium. Milan’s current stadium — one of the most iconic in European football and often likened to a “concrete cathedral” — is the largest in Italy. But the venue, which opened in 1926, no longer meets the needs of spectators or the clubs, despite undergoing several renovations over the decades. San Siro, also known as the Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, will be largely demolished once construction work on the new stadium nears completion. items.title: Trade Ministry launches pharmaceutical policy to double local medicine production
items.description: The government has launched the Cabinet-approved Ghana Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Policy, seeking to double domestic medicine production, create skilled jobs and position the country as a leading pharmaceutical manufacturing hub in West Africa. The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, announced the policy at its launch in Accra on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. She said the policy was designed to address Ghana’s dependence on imported medicines, which currently account for about 70% of the country’s medicine supply. Under the policy, Ghana aims to increase the share of locally manufactured medicines in the domestic market from 30 per cent to 60 per cent, as an intermediate step towards President John Mahama’s target of achieving 70 per cent local pharmaceutical self-sufficiency. “Medicines are not ordinary goods. A country that cannot produce its own essential medicines leaves its health, economy, and sovereignty vulnerable,” Mrs Ofosu-Adjare said. She explained that the policy would provide a coordinated framework to align investment, regulation, public procurement, skills development and regional trade in support of local pharmaceutical manufacturers. The Minister outlined six key pillars underpinning the policy, including improving the quality of locally manufactured medicines to meet international standards, expanding market access for domestic producers and providing affordable, long-term financing. The government also plans to support local manufacturers to obtain World Health Organisation Good Manufacturing Practice certification and prequalification, while using public procurement and the National Health Insurance Scheme to prioritise quality medicines produced in Ghana. On financing, Mrs Ofosu-Adjare said the policy would promote partnerships with Development Bank Ghana, Ghana EXIM Bank and GIPA to improve access to long-term funding for pharmaceutical businesses. The policy also seeks to move the industry beyond packaging into the production of active pharmaceutical ingredients, excipients and vaccines. Other priorities include strengthening collaboration between academia and industry, equipping clinical pharmacists with skills for pharmaceutical manufacturing, and expanding exports through the African Continental Free Trade Area and the Economic Community of West African States. The launch brought together representatives from key institutions involved in the policy’s implementation, including the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Finance, Food and Drugs Authority, National Vaccine Institute, Development Bank Ghana, GIZ, the World Health Organisation and the European Union. The government expects the policy to strengthen local manufacturing capacity, reduce dependence on imported medicines and create opportunities for Ghanaian pharmaceutical businesses to expand into regional markets.

items.title: Pakistan 'overperformer' in innovation, climbs 4 ranks globally in 2026: report
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan rose to 95th place among the 139 economies of the world featured in the ‘Global Innovation Index 2026’ published by the World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO), it emerged on Thursday. Advancing in rank from 99th place in 2025, Pakistan also reclaimed its “overperformer” status for the fourth time, a status given to economies identified as performing above expectations for their level of economic development. It also held the status in 2022 and 2024. The global index report showed that Pakistan performed better in innovation outputs than innovation inputs in 2026. This year, Pakistan ranked 121st in innovation inputs and 72nd in innovation outputs — both higher than last year. “Innovation overperformance shows that innovation does not follow a straight line from income to results,” the report said. “The 2026 overperformers show that economies can generate more innovation than expected for their level of development when they build on focused strengths.” A list of countries that performed above expectations for their level of development in innovation in 2026, according to the Global Innovation Index 2026. — screengrab from WIPO report WIPO highlighted that Pakistan’s strengths were concentrated in the digital economy , particularly mobile app creation, ICT services exports, high-tech imports, and software spending. It added that the country’s “relatively strong” scientific production and university quality supported a developing digital economy. In the 2026 index, Pakistan ranked 15th among the 36 lower middle-income group economies and eighth among the 11 economies in central and southern Asia. It did not rank among the top innovation clusters in any specific innovation pillar of the index (including ‘human capital and research’, ‘infrastructure’, etc). This partial screengrab from WIPO report shows Pakistan ranks 95th overall and does not rank among leading countries in any innovation pillar, in Global Innovation Index 2026. Pakistan’s GII ranking (2020-2026) showed a rise over the past seven years, ranking 107th in 2020; 99th in 2021; 87th in 2022; 88th in 2023; 91st in 2024; and 99th in 2025. Meanwhile, Switzerland, Sweden and the United States remained the world’s top three innovation economies, with Switzerland ranking first for a 16th consecutive year. The organisation noted, “In a period of major geopolitical and economic turbulence, the most striking feature about the top of the ranking is its stability.” According to the report, the leading economies broadly remain the same as in 2025, with no new economy in the top 15 since last year, and Europe once more accounting for the largest share of the group with 14 economies out of 25 innovation leaders. Additionally, the Netherlands moved up to seventh place and Austria to 18th. “The main signal at the innovation frontier this year is continuity, rather than the emergence of any single new entrant,” the report said. Five Asian economies were also among the top 25: South Korea and Singapore in fourth and fifth place respectively; China remaining 10th — as the only middle-income economy among the innovation leaders — Japan at 12th and Hong Kong, China in 14th place. The report highlighted that the presence of Asian economies was now an “established feature of the top ranks, rather than a development unique to this year”. According to the report, the GII 2026 Innovation Tracker pointed to “continued but slower progress across the innovation cycle”. Most indicators advanced, with notable gains in scientific output, corporate research and development (R&D), battery costs and technology adoption; however, about three-quarters remained below the decade average. Research effort nonetheless remained at a historic high, it pointed out, with global R&D intensity close to two per cent of GDP. The WIPO report identified that the near-term environment was more demanding than the previous year: “Global growth of about 3.4pc in 2025 is expected to ease to around 3pc in 2026, held back by higher energy prices and elevated uncertainty, before recovering modestly in 2027.” It highlighted that AI-related investment remained “the main engine on the upside”, with the largest hyper-scalers set to spend over $1 trillion on AI infrastructure across 2025 and 2026. “This will be increasingly financed through debt and private credit, meaning a downward revision of expected AI returns could tighten financing conditions well beyond the sector,” it added. The report noted that emerging economies, including Pakistan, could build on their standout strengths to improve their overall innovation performance.

items.title: Ghana woos Polish investors with access to African markets
items.description: Ghana has urged Polish and other European businesses to invest in the country, citing its democratic stability, access to African markets and improving economic conditions as key advantages. The Deputy Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Sampson Ahi, made the call during a panel discussion on “What Investors Need to Know from Both Governments” at the TOP CHARITY ChangeMAKERS Africa Business Mixer in Accra. He said Ghana’s stable democratic environment, respect for the rule of law and growing middle class made it an attractive destination for investors seeking to expand their operations. Mr Ahi also highlighted Ghana’s role as host of the Secretariat of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), describing it as a strategic advantage for businesses seeking access to the wider African market. The AfCFTA provides a framework for trade across 54 African countries, representing a potential market of approximately 1.4 billion people. He encouraged Polish and other European businesses to explore investment opportunities in Ghana, particularly as the government pursues efforts to strengthen the country’s industrial base, create jobs and deepen international trade relations. The Deputy Minister said greater investment would support Ghana’s economic ambitions while creating opportunities for stronger commercial partnerships between Ghanaian and European businesses.

items.title: Maroc : le prix de la tomate s’envole, jusqu’à 11 dirhams le kilo
items.description: Les prix de la tomate connaissent une forte hausse sur les marchés de gros au Maroc, atteignant jusqu’à 8 dirhams le kilogramme pour les produits de bonne qualité. Les professionnels attribuent cette flambée à la baisse de la production et à la hausse des coûts agricoles, tout en écartant la responsabilité des exportations. La tomate devient de plus en plus chère sur les marchés marocains. À Meknès, le prix du kilogramme peut atteindre 8 dirhams sur le marché de gros, avant de grimper entre 10 et 11 dirhams chez les détaillants pour les produits de bonne qualité. Une hausse qui s’explique principalement par la baisse de l’offre, selon plusieurs professionnels du secteur. La flambée des prix concerne particulièrement les tomates de qualité supérieure. À Meknès, les tarifs des caisses ont fortement augmenté, oscillant désormais entre 150 et 200 dirhams, selon les professionnels interrogés par Hespress . Hicham Meknassi, professionnel au marché de gros des fruits et légumes de Meknès, explique cette situation par le recul de la production locale. La fin de la période de production dans la région des Doukkala, conjuguée au retard de maturation des récoltes dans le Souss, réduit les quantités disponibles sur les marchés. À cette diminution de l’offre s’ajoute une demande soutenue, contribuant au maintien de prix élevés. Les frais de transport, les pertes de marchandises et les marges des détaillants accentuent également l’écart entre les prix de gros et ceux payés par les consommateurs. Contrairement à la tomate, d’autres produits, comme l’oignon, affichent une relative stabilité des prix. Les professionnels écartent la responsabilité des exportations Alors que les exportations sont régulièrement mises en cause lors des hausses des prix des produits agricoles, les professionnels interrogés estiment qu’elles ne constituent pas le principal facteur de la flambée actuelle. Hicham Meknassi affirme que les opérateurs de l’export souffrent eux-mêmes d’un manque de marchandises, en raison de la baisse des volumes disponibles dans les exploitations agricoles. De son côté, Abdelaziz Maânaoui, président de l’Association des producteurs agricoles de Chtouka, souligne que les prix varient sensiblement selon la qualité des tomates. Sur les marchés de gros, ils peuvent aller de 3 dirhams le kilogramme pour les produits de qualité inférieure à 10 dirhams pour les meilleures catégories. Il appelle ainsi à distinguer les différentes catégories de produits avant de généraliser les constats sur la hausse des prix. Selon lui, les exportateurs destineraient, dans les situations les plus importantes, entre 50 % et 60% de la production aux marchés étrangers, tandis que le reste serait orienté vers le marché national, conformément aux critères appliqués au secteur. Au-delà des fluctuations saisonnières, la filière fait face à des difficultés structurelles. Les professionnels évoquent notamment la propagation d’un virus affectant les plants de tomates et réduisant les rendements, malgré le recours à de nouvelles variétés résistantes. La hausse des prix des intrants agricoles, des engrais et de la main-d’œuvre pèse également sur la rentabilité des exploitations. Selon Abdelaziz Maânaoui, cultiver un hectare de tomates représente désormais un investissement risqué, susceptible d’entraîner des pertes importantes. Cette situation inciterait certains agriculteurs à réduire leurs surfaces cultivées ou à renoncer à cette production, contribuant ainsi à la contraction de l’offre. Pour les professionnels, la sortie de crise passe notamment par des mécanismes de soutien aux agriculteurs et par des mesures encourageant l’augmentation de la production. L’objectif est de garantir un approvisionnement suffisant du marché national et de limiter les tensions sur les prix. En attendant une amélioration des volumes disponibles, les consommateurs restent confrontés à une hausse du prix d’un produit incontournable de leur alimentation quotidienne. The post Maroc : le prix de la tomate s’envole, jusqu’à 11 dirhams le kilo appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: 2027: INEC grants provisional clearance to Pantami, Gwarzo – Source
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi & Ben Ngwakwe There were strong indications on Thursday night that the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC might have provisionally cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Gombe State, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections. The clearance of both men is subject to the outcome of pending court cases, it was learned on Thursday night. In Gombe, Pantami’s supporters took over some major areas celebrating the development on Thursday night. INEC officials did not immediately react to Vanguard’s questions regarding the development. But a source said the decisions were reached at the commission’s meeting on Thursday to consider complaints from political parties and candidates whose names were left out of the lists published ahead of the 2027 elections. The source added that the commission had no objection to their candidacies, but that the pending legal proceedings could still affect the final outcome. The development comes after INEC dropped Pantami’s name from the final list of governorship candidates for Gombe State, although he appeared on the provisional list published on August 29. Pantami emerged as the PDP candidate after leaving the All Progressives Congress (APC) on May 19. One of the aspirants for the ticket, Ahmed Mailantarki Mailantarki, challenged his victory in court. A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which Pantami won again. His biggest hurdle was the September 24 Supreme Court judgement, which restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. The provisions bar parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time. Mohammed Haruna, an INEC National Commissioner, had previously said that, in line with the Supreme Court ruling, some parties would not field candidates in 2027. The commission, however, rejected a petition by the PDP governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, who had asked it to review his exclusion from the list of candidates. items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : un centre de contrôle installé pour une vision consolidée du trafic routier
items.description: Un centre de contrôle dénommé Transport Operations Center (TROC) a été installé jeudi au siège du Conseil exécutif des Transports urbains durables (Cetud). Le but est, selon le ministre des Transports terrestres et aériens, Abdoul Ahad Ndiaye, d’offrir une vision consolidée du trafic et d'assurer une réactivité optimale face aux aléas de la circulation, notamment dans le cadre des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (Dakar 2026). À l'approche des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026, le ministre des Transports terrestres et aériens, Abdoul Ahad Ndiaye a présidé le jeudi 29 octobre 2026, au siège du Conseil exécutif des Transports urbains durables (Cetud), la cérémonie d'installation officielle du Transport Operations Center (TROC). « En présence des autorités administratives, des représentants du COJOJ, des forces de défense et de sécurité ainsi que de l'ensemble des acteurs de la mobilité, j'ai réaffirmé l'enjeu stratégique des transports pour la réussite de ce rendez-vous mondial : garantir à nos hôtes, aux délégations, aux volontaires et aux populations des déplacements fluides, sécurisés et ponctuels », a expliqué le ministre. A lire aussi : JOJ Dakar 2026 : 30 ambulances mobilisées, plus de 600 professionnels de santé identifiés « Conçu comme une véritable tour de contrôle, le TROC a pour vocation de fédérer l'ensemble de nos structures opérationnelles afin de nous offrir une vision consolidée du trafic et d'assurer une réactivité optimale face aux aléas de la circulation », a-t-il ajouté. Par ailleurs, tout en saluant le travail accompli par le Cetud et les comités techniques sur les plans de transport, de circulation et de stationnement, le ministre a insisté sur l'exigence d'une anticipation rigoureuse et d'une coordination sans faille avant de déclarer le centre officiellement installé. items.title: War’s scars and hope for healing: Sudanese stories through the art of Amani Azhari
items.description: Through her series Healing Sessions , Sudanese visual artist Amani Azhari explores women’s experiences of war and trauma, tracing their emotions and the transformations in their lives through art. Drawing on the traditional gatherings of women in Sudanese homes, she creates space for sharing, mutual support, and psychological healing, while giving expression to the individual and collective wounds left by the war. Azhari’s paintings portray women in different physical poses, with their expressions and ways of sitting conveying pain, loneliness, comfort, and contemplation. Everyday details also reveal the demands placed on women and the burdens they carry. Speaking to Radio Dabanga from her studio in Nairobi, the artist says her interest in these scenes began in childhood, when she observed how women sat together, interacted, and used their bodies to express sadness and joy. Healing Sessions : spaces for recovering from trauma Azhari began working on the Healing Sessions series after war broke out in Sudan, when she was living in Kampala, Uganda, before moving to Kenya. She describes that period as one of shock and isolation, particularly because she was separated from her Sudanese community and lacked a close social and artistic network in her new surroundings. The war, she explains, inflicted widespread trauma on Sudanese people. But these wounds did not begin with the fighting: they had accumulated through earlier experiences endured by Sudanese society. Through Healing Sessions , Azhari brought together Sudanese people living abroad and began listening to their accounts of what they had experienced during the war — the fear, pain, and loss. Some participants cried or shouted as they spoke, while others chose simply to listen. Their responses prompted her to reflect on the psychological impact of these experiences, and on how conversation and sharing can help people understand their feelings and make sense of what is happening around them. Azhari sees traditional women’s gatherings in Sudan as a form of informal psychological support, even if the women taking part would not necessarily describe them as therapy. Her work recalls gatherings of grandmothers, aunts, and other female relatives in family homes, where women can speak freely, exchange experiences, drink coffee, and unburden themselves away from outside interference. She describes these gatherings as intimate and almost sacred spaces, offering a sense of safety, belonging, and solidarity. Healing Sesions Motherhood between love and responsibility The Healing Sessions paintings do not portray women only in moments of rest or social connection. They also explore the psychological and social dimensions of motherhood, the difficult balance between caring for children and working, and the changes and responsibilities that reshape a woman’s life. One painting depicts a mother and child in a moment of intimacy and protection, while the child appears to be watching what is happening around them. For Azhari, motherhood is not simply a matter of love and care: it demands considerable effort and responsibility, and brings profound changes to a woman’s life. She explains that the transition from childhood, or from a life in which a woman is cared for by her family, to one in which she must shoulder responsibility herself can happen suddenly. This is particularly true during war, displacement, and exile, when women may find themselves facing the demands of daily life alone. Azhari reflects on women forced to leave their homes and communities, losing the presence of relatives, friends, and the support networks on which they had relied. Some find themselves dealing with pregnancy, childbirth, and raising children in unfamiliar surroundings, far from their families — sometimes without anyone who speaks their language or shares the details of their everyday lives. Azhari’s paintings also draw on her own suffering and experience after the war. She faced pregnancy and childbirth without her husband or family beside her. Her work therefore reflects the profound changes women undergo in different circumstances, as well as the personal experiences that shape her artistic vision. In her interview with Radio Dabanga, she says that placing women at the centre of her work is a way of expressing herself, but also reflects her awareness of the burdens Sudanese women carry during the war: displacement, exile, family responsibilities, and the struggle to rebuild their lives. One of the most prominent works in the series is a large painting measuring three meters by three meters, designed by the artist so that the painted figures appear as if they are actually sitting on a sofa in front of the viewer The sofa: a witness to memory and change One of the series’ most striking works is a large painting, measuring three metres by three metres, in which the artist makes the figures appear to be sitting on a real sofa in front of the viewer. The sofa occupies a central place in Azhari’s work. It is more than a piece of furniture: it becomes a witness to the changes experienced by the figures, preserving the traces of their encounters, conversations, and emotions. For Azhari, it has become something like an archive or an outside observer, recording the details and transformations unfolding around it. The way the women sit, the distances between them, and the cushions and objects surrounding them all carry meanings beyond their outward appearance. In the visual language of Azhari’s work, the sofa becomes a silent stage for the soul. Women sit alongside one another as thoughts gather before they are spoken. Some bodies rest, others collapse, while others seem to float in the air like memories that have slipped free of gravity. Their gazes meet ours with a dreamy boredom or quiet defiance, as though the painting has captured the moment after an event, when everything has fallen silent except the heart. Colour is freed from the obligation to imitate reality. Lemon yellow and fuchsia pink become languages of feeling rather than skin tones. Deep blue meets fiery orange in a dialogue between night and embers, while decorative patterns — dots, flowers, and patches of colour — become a musical rhythm flowing across fabrics, walls, and sofas. One of the artist’s most compelling choices is to leave the preparatory drawing visible above the flat areas of colour. The paintings seem to breathe as they take shape, making the first marks part of the story itself. There are distant echoes of Paul Gauguin’s symbolic use of colour, Henri Matisse’s decorative flattening of warm interiors, Marc Chagall’s dreamlike figures in flight, and Pablo Picasso’s simplification and distortion of form. Yet Azhari draws on these influences only where they serve her own world, creating a distinctive visual language of silent intimacy, waiting, and the beautiful exhaustion of life at home. Azhari tells Radio Dabanga that these details of domestic space are inseparable from memory and emotion. The places where people spend their time hold the experiences they have lived through, and the moments of happiness, sadness, and change that have shaped them. The series includes a large work measuring three metres by three metres. Azhari designed it so that the painted figures appear to be sitting on an actual sofa in front of the viewer. The intention is to bring the audience closer to the scene, giving them the sensation of being inside the room rather than simply looking at a painting hanging on a wall. The room within me: the Sudan we carry with us Alongside Healing Sessions , Azhari explores displacement and separation from home in a painting entitled The Room Inside Me. The work considers the idea that Sudan is not merely a geographical place, but an inner space that people carry with them wherever they go. Azhari explains that this symbolic room contains childhood memories, the details of everyday life, customs, traditions, and values that shape a person’s life and identity. Even when Sudanese people leave their homeland because of war or exile, these details remain present in their memories and influence how they understand the world around them. The painting includes objects and elements drawn from Azhari’s own memories and personal experience. They suggest that what people carry from their homeland extends beyond material possessions to include emotions, experiences, and relationships that remain with them despite the distance. For Azhari, this offers a way to explore the relationship between people and their homeland that goes beyond geography, encompassing what lives on in memory and the inner self, and what continues to shape life even after leaving home. Art as a message against war Azhari has also taken part in initiatives using art to raise awareness of the war in Sudan and call for an end to the fighting. Among them is the Barddoha campaign. As part of the campaign, she created a large artwork in the shape of a clock whose hands had stopped at 13 April. The image represents the moment when life stood still under the weight of war. In place of the clock’s conventional hands, she used an inverted rifle — a reference to the misuse of weapons that should protect people and their country but have instead become instruments of destruction and harm. The work was exhibited during the Berlin conference, with the aim of conveying a visual message about the war in Sudan and prompting discussion about its consequences and the need to end it. Azhari tells Radio Dabanga that she developed the idea while searching for an artistic form capable of conveying several messages in a single image, rather than relying solely on placards and written slogans. Through the stopped clock and inverted rifle, she sought to express the feeling that time had come to a halt in Sudan while people’s suffering continued. The artist is also taking part in workshops and discussion sessions with civil society representatives, exploring what art can contribute to addressing the consequences of war and how artists can participate in wider discussions and efforts to respond to the crisis. Azhari has participated in group exhibitions featuring artists from across East Africa. At one of these exhibitions, she was the only Sudanese artist, presenting two paintings from the Healing Sessions series. She has also discussed other artistic engagements, including exhibitions scheduled for October, among them one at the residence of the German ambassador in Kenya. These appearances form part of her effort to bring Sudanese experiences to a wider audience and draw attention to the psychological and social changes people are undergoing as a result of war and displacement. Her message to Sudanese people is one of hope. She hopes they will not lose heart, and that they will remember that life continues despite the harshest circumstances. Confronting the effects of war requires people to comfort one another, understand themselves, and discover what each person can contribute. It is essential, she says, to preserve one’s passion and continue looking towards the future, without allowing painful experiences to extinguish the desire to live, work, and create. A diverse series of works by visual artist Amani Azhari in her studio in Nairobi, Kenya (Photos by Radio Dabanga) Share article The post War’s scars and hope for healing: Sudanese stories through the art of Amani Azhari appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

items.title: Algérie : saisie géante de psychotropes, le parquet dévoile les noms de 10 suspects
items.description: Nouvelle opération d’envergure contre les réseaux de trafic de stupéfiants en Algérie. Dix personnes soupçonnées d’être impliquées dans une affaire de trafic de 2,4 millions comprimés psychotropes ont été placées sous mandat de dépôt ce jeudi sur ordre du juge d'instruction près le pôle pénal national de lutte contre le terrorisme et la criminalité organisée transnationale du tribunal de Sidi M'hamed. « Conformément aux dispositions de l'article 19 du Code de procédure pénale et de l'article 34 bis1 de la loi 25-03 modifiant et complétant la loi 04-18 relative à la prévention et à la répression de l'usage et du trafic illicites de stupéfiants et de substances psychotropes, le parquet près le pôle pénal national de lutte contre le terrorisme et la criminalité organisée transnationale du tribunal de Sidi M'hamed porte à la connaissance de l'opinion publique que suite à l'enquête préliminaire menée par le service central de lutte contre le trafic illicite de drogues et de substances psychotropes de la Sûreté nationale, un groupe criminel organisé composé de 15 individus a été arrêté », a indiqué le parquet dans un communiqué. Affaire des 2,4 millions de comprimés psychotropes : les noms de 10 suspects dévoilés Dix personnes de ce groupe ont été « prises en flagrant délit », a précisé le parquet qui a dévoilé leur identité. Il s'agit de Rachid Merabet (44 ans), Hocine Touil (37 ans), Nabil Ghazal (32 ans), Fouad Ghazal (29 ans), Nassim Touil (39 ans), Ahamed Benaziza (37 ans), Akram Benaziza (26 ans), Oussama Tifoura (31 ans), Ziad Asnine, surnommé « Essalk » (23 ans) et Idriss Gharbi (44 ans), selon la même source. « L’identité des cinq autres individus en fuite a été établie », a précisé le parquet. Lors de cette opération, 2,4 millions de comprimés psychotropes de type Prégabaline (300 mg), qui se trouvaient en « possession des individus interpellés », a été saisie, selon la même source. A la suite de la présentation des mis en cause devant le parquet de la République ce jeudi, des poursuites ont été engagées à leur encontre dans le cadre d'une instruction judiciaire pour les chefs d’inculpation d’ « importation, transport, transit, stockage et détention illicites de substances psychotropes pour trafic, dans le cadre d'une organisation criminelle transnationale visant à porter atteinte à la sécurité nationale et à l’ordre public et à créer un climat d'insécurité, outre le crime de contrebande d'une gravité majeure menaçant la sécurité et la santé publiques, ainsi que le blanchiment de capitaux en bande organisée », ajoute le communiqué. A l'issue de l'interrogatoire des 10 individus arrêtés, le juge d'instruction a ordonné leur placement en détention provisoire. L’article Algérie : saisie géante de psychotropes, le parquet dévoile les noms de 10 suspects est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Le RNI réunit son 8è congrès pour redéfinir la stratégie du parti
items.description: Le Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI) devrait se réunir en congrès national sous la présidence de Rachid Talbi Alami dans les prochaines semaines pour faire le bilan des dernières échéances électorales et poursuivre sa réorganisation annoncée post-scrutin. Une commission préparatoire a été mise en route pour poser les jalons de son huitième congrès national, prévu les 22 et 23 janvier prochains, a annoncé le parti qui dirigeait le gouvernement pendant cinq ans avant de passer à l'opposition au termes du dernier scrutin de septembre. Même si le parti avait annoncé sa volonté de participer au gouvernement, le choix final de la composition de la majorité n'avait pas retenu le parti de la « Colombe ». Le congrès national du RNI devrait se tenir sous la présidence de Rachid Talbi Alami, a annoncé le parti dans un communiqué. La commission de préparation du congrès s’inscrit dans la poursuite de la dynamique organisationnelle et le renforcement de la pratique démocratique interne, indique le document. Le parti avait déjà annoncé son intention d'opérer des changements et de faire le bilan des élections du 23 septembre dernier. Le RNI s'est classé deuxième derrière le Parti Authenticité et Modernité (PAM). Lors du scrutin de 2021, le RNI avait remporté 102 sièges contre 66 sièges lors de ces dernières échéances électorales. Le parti avait annoncé sa volonté de tirer les enseignements de son expérience gouvernementale et de son recul électoral, tout en redéfinissant sa stratégie politique et organisationnelle pour s’adapter à son nouveau statut de parti d’opposition. A l'issue des résultats, le chef de file du RNI, Mohamed Chouki avait déclaré que de même que le parti était fier de la confiance des citoyens lorsque leurs résultats progressent, ils devaient également « écouter attentivement leur message lorsqu’ils reculent », en affirmant qu’il s’agit pour son parti, d’une règle fondamentale de la pratique démocratique et du respect de la volonté des électeurs. Le 3 octobre, lors de la tenue du Conseil national du RNI réuni en session extraordinaire, le parti avait affirmé dans un communiqué que les résultats obtenus lors des dernières élections, malgré le recul enregistré, « constituent une expression claire et concrète du fait que le Rassemblement national des indépendants demeure une véritable force politique, disposant de tous les atouts nécessaires pour résister, assurer sa continuité et tirer les enseignements de cette expérience ». A cette occasion, Mohamed Chouki, a déclaré dans un discours que « revenir sur le parcours du parti constitue une étape importante que nous ne voulons pas réduire à un simple moment d’évaluation, mais plutôt en faire un point de départ permettant de tourner la page de l’échéance électorale ». Le chef du RNI avait alors estimé que le recul électoral était une réalité politique qui ne devait être « ni dissimulée ni minimisée dans sa portée », et de souligner que la politique ne consistait pas uniquement à savoir accueillir le succès, mais qu’elle exigeait également de savoir analyser les périodes de recul. « Le Rassemblement national des indépendants se prépare, dès à présent, aux prochaines échéances politiques et organisationnelles, avec une vision claire, une volonté collective et une pleine responsabilité » , avait-t-il affirmé, rappelant que les cinq années durant lesquelles son parti a assumé la responsabilité de diriger le gouvernement, « n’ont pas été des années ordinaires » compte tenu des défis nationaux et internationaux successifs, parallèlement à la mise en œuvre de réformes et à la réponse à d’importantes attentes sociales et économiques. The post Le RNI réunit son 8è congrès pour redéfinir la stratégie du parti appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Health Minister assures public of Ghana’s readiness to respond to Ebola
items.description: The Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, has assured the public that Ghana is prepared to detect and respond to any potential Ebola case, following an inspection of screening and emergency response measures at Accra International Airport. He said Ghana had not recorded any Ebola case and urged the public to remain calm, noting that the government had strengthened surveillance and response systems to protect the country against the disease. Mr Akandoh explained that, in the absence of a specific treatment or vaccine for the Ebola strain of concern, early detection, contact tracing and effective containment were critical to preventing its spread. As part of the preventive measures, he said thermal scanners had been installed at the airport to screen arriving passengers for symptoms that could indicate an infection. The Minister also disclosed that electronic health declaration forms were being finalised to enable passengers travelling to Ghana to submit relevant health information before arrival. According to him, the system would help health officials assess travellers and identify those who may require further investigation. He said the Ministry would soon issue an official statement on the implementation of the electronic declaration system, after which airlines and airport authorities would be expected to ensure that passengers completed the forms. Mr Akandoh added that designated facilities were available for the isolation and treatment of patients should a case be detected. “We are ready, and we are praying we don’t record any case, but if we do, we are ready to do the needful,” he said. He stressed that all arriving passengers must comply with the required screening procedures, regardless of their status. The Minister further disclosed that the government was expanding screening capacity at the country’s land borders as part of broader efforts to strengthen Ghana’s defences against infectious diseases.

items.title: ‘Star Trek’, ‘X-Men’ star Patrick Stewart dies at 86
items.description: Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died at the age of 86, an official statement said Thursday. “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement said. The actor, who hailed from the northern English region of Yorkshire, trod the boards in Britain with the Royal Shakespeare Company before crossing the Atlantic to enjoy an acclaimed career on the US stage and screen. His best known Hollywood roles were as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and Professor Charles Xavier in multiple “X-Men” and related Marvel films. “His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the statement said. “He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.” AFP The post ‘Star Trek’, ‘X-Men’ star Patrick Stewart dies at 86 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Health Minister urges contractors to speed up La General Hospital project

Mr Akandoh said the hospital was expected to serve a large population, making timely completion critical to improving access to healthcare. He dismissed delays in government payments as an excuse for slow progress, insisting that contractors had been paid on time. He added that the latest interim payment certificate had been submitted and forwarded to the Ministry of Finance for processing. The Minister also called for a review of the proposed capacity of the hospital’s emergency department to ensure it could meet demand and help address challenges associated with the availability of emergency beds. The €50 million project includes the provision and installation of medical equipment. Mr Akandoh pledged that the government would continue to monitor construction until the facility was completed and operational.

items.title: Responsible mining must be the standard, not the exception – Dr Zanetor Rawlings
items.description: The Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, has called for responsible mining practices to become the standard in Ghana, stressing that mineral extraction must not come at the expense of the environment. She made the call after visiting Zijin Mining’s operations at New Abirem in the Eastern Region as part of a field tour to assess the environmental impact of mining activities. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings said the visit presented a contrast to the environmental destruction she witnessed at illegal mining sites in Osino, demonstrating that mining could be conducted responsibly with deliberate measures to minimise damage and restore degraded areas. During the visit, she said, officials of the mining company took her through their environmental management practices, including land reclamation, the rehabilitation of mined-out areas and tree planting initiatives aimed at protecting and restoring the environment. The Minister acknowledged the importance of Ghana’s mineral resources to economic development but cautioned against extraction practices that threaten water bodies, farmlands and ecosystems. She stressed that protecting the environment was essential to safeguarding the wellbeing of future generations. “Our mineral resources are important to Ghana’s economic development, but their extraction must never come at the expense of our water bodies, farmlands, ecosystems and the wellbeing of future generations,” she said. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings insisted that responsible mining should not be treated as an exception but adopted as the standard across the sector. “Responsible mining must not be the exception. It must be the standard,” she added.

items.title: Troops neutralise two high-profile ISWAP leaders, others in Borno
items.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The troops of Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have killed 15 Boko Haram terrorists, including two (2) prominent ISWAP Qayids, Abu Musanna and Hassan Abu Huraira in Kerenoa, Marte Local Government Area of Borno State. This is as the Theatre Commander of OPHK, Major General Ibikunle Ajose on Thursday commissioned the newly constructed three blocks of 12-family Corporals and Below Quarters (CBQ) at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri. The commissioning forms part of activities to commemorate the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu’s one year in office, which also reflects his commitment to improving troops’ living conditions, strengthening morale and enhancing operational effectiveness. In a press statement signed by the Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni on Thursday said: “Troops of OPHK continued to record operational successes through sustained intelligence-led offensive operations aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities and dismantling their networks across the theatre. “In a further operation, OPHK air assets, at about 9:20 pm on 28 October 2026, conducted an armed reconnaissance and air interdiction mission in the Kerenoa Marte Local Government Area of Borno State, resulting in the neutralisation of 15 terrorists and the destruction of an IED hideout. “The mission followed intelligence reports on terrorist activities in the area. During the operation, the air assets tracked two terrorists on a motorcycle to a makeshift structure beneath a tree. Further surveillance revealed additional movements around the location, indicating the presence of other terrorists. Consequently, the location was engaged with precision strikes. “Following the strikes, Battle Damage Assessment (BDA) indicated that 15 terrorists were neutralised, while structures at the location were destroyed. Additionally, a secondary fire observed after the engagement suggested that the targeted structure may have been used for the storage of terrorist IED logistics hub. “It has been confirmed that 2 prominent ISWAP Qayids, Abu Musanna and Hassan Abu Huraira were amongst those neutralised while several other fighters were severely wounded, including the Wali (ISWAP Governor) of the area who is reported to be critically injured. “The operation forms part of OPHK’s sustained intelligence-led air offensive aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities, disrupting their hideouts and dismantling logistics networks across the theatre. The Joint Task Force continues to conduct coordinated operations against terrorist elements in the North East to achieve its Operational mandate of restoring total and long-lasting peace in the region,” Goni stated. Meanwhile, the Nigerian Army has reaffirmed its commitment to personnel welfare with the commissioning of three blocks of 12-family Corporals and Below Quarters (CBQ) at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri. The commissioning reflects the commitment of the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu NAM, to improving troops’ living conditions, strengthening morale and enhancing operational effectiveness. The commissioning forms part of activities to commemorate the COAS one year in office. The COAS was represented at the ceremony by the Theatre Commander, Joint Task Force (North East) Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), Major General Ibikunle Ajose, on Thursday, 29 October 2026, at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri. Delivering the COAS’ remarks, Major General Ajose stated that decent accommodation and a conducive living environment were essential to sustaining troops’ morale, discipline and effectiveness. He emphasised that operational excellence on the battlefield must be supported by adequate welfare provisions and a strong administrative foundation at home. He described investments in accommodation as investments in human capital and a practical demonstration of the Nigerian Army’s appreciation of personnel’s sacrifices and contributions to national security. The COAS expressed profound appreciation to the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, for his continued support to the Nigerian Army, particularly in force development and personnel welfare. He also acknowledged the contributions of relevant departments and directorates, contractors, project supervisors and other stakeholders whose efforts supported the execution of the projects, noting that sustained institutional support remains vital to the Army’s transformation and operational effectiveness. The COAS charged beneficiary personnel and their commanders to maintain a strong culture of discipline, accountability and proper maintenance to preserve the facilities for long-term use. The commissioning reinforces the Nigerian Army’s Soldiers First Concept, which places the welfare, wellbeing and professional development of personnel at the centre of its institutional priorities and recognises their importance to sustained morale, operational readiness and effective service to the nation. Beyond the quarters commissioned, several other projects are ongoing at Maimalari Cantonment to improve living and working conditions. These include additional Corporals and Below Quarters, the drilling of two boreholes, construction of a 50-bed ward for 7 Division Medical Services and Hospital, a new Headquarters 7 Division complex, Senior Officers’ Quarters and the renovation of existing family accommodation. These interventions reflect broader efforts to strengthen military infrastructure and provide personnel and their families with improved housing, healthcare and essential facilities. In his welcome address, the Acting General Officer Commanding 7 Division and Commander Sector 1 OPHK, Brigadier General Solomon Diwa, described the commissioning as another significant milestone in the Army’s welfare initiatives. He noted that Corporals and Below constitute a vital component of the Army’s fighting strength and perform indispensable roles at the tactical level. He stressed that providing them with decent accommodation demonstrates the Army’s recognition of their service and sacrifices while reinforcing the connection between personnel welfare, high morale and combat readiness. Similarly, the Acting GOC urged occupants to uphold high standards of cleanliness, take ownership of the quarters and ensure their responsible use. In his project description, the Commander, 47 Engineer Brigade, Brigadier General Abubakar Saleh, disclosed that the renovation was awarded to Messrs Ammah Contractors Limited by the Office of the Chief of Army Staff, Directorate of Procurement. He explained that following a site assessment, six blocks of six-family Corporals and Below Quarters, comprising 36 two-bedroom flats, were selected for renovation as suitable alternatives to the originally designated structures. He noted that the buildings were previously in a severely dilapidated condition, with leaking roofs, structural cracks and damaged floors. The renovation involved extensive structural rehabilitation, including the introduction of columns and beams, repairs to damaged floor slabs and masonry, replacement of roofing sheets, doors and windows, and complete electrical and plumbing installations. He added that 47 Engineer Brigade supervised the project under the guidance of Headquarters 7 Division to ensure compliance with approved specifications and quality standards. While delivering the vote of thanks on behalf of the beneficiaries, Warrant Officer Ogunmodede Sunday expressed his sincere appreciation to the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, NAM, for prioritising personnel welfare through the Soldiers First Concept. He also thanked the Theatre Commander for his leadership and for representing the COAS at the occasion. He noted that the renovated quarters and other ongoing infrastructure projects demonstrate the Nigerian Army’s commitment to improving personnel welfare and living conditions. He pledged that the beneficiaries would maintain the facilities responsibly and reciprocate the gesture through discipline, professionalism and dedication to duty. He concluded by appreciating the project supervisors, contractors and everyone who contributed to the success of the project, while praying for God’s continued protection of troops, blessings upon their families and lasting peace and security for Nigeria. The post Troops neutralise two high-profile ISWAP leaders, others in Borno appeared first on Vanguard News .
