items.title: African CEOs remain confident in growth, but economic uncertainty, AI readiness will shape next phase of investment – KPMG
items.description: African business leaders remain confident about growth, but converting that confidence into sustained performance will depend on how effectively organisations navigate economic uncertainty, geopolitical disruption, technological change and structural constraints, according to the 2026 KPMG Africa CEO Outlook. The third edition of the KPMG Africa CEO Outlook examines the priorities shaping business leadership across the continent, from investment and growth expectations to emerging risks, artificial intelligence (AI), talent and sustainability. The findings point to a business environment in which ambition remains strong, but execution is becoming increasingly important. While 66% of African CEOs are confident in the global economy, broadly in line with the global benchmark of 65%, confidence in their domestic economies stands at 72%. A further 79% are confident in the growth prospects of their own organisations. This confidence is supported by recent performance, with 86% of African CEOs reporting revenue growth in their latest financial year. However, only 58% expect annual earnings growth of at least 2.5% over the next three years, compared with 68% globally, suggesting that translating revenue gains into sustained profitability remains a priority. Economic uncertainty reinforces the need for resilience African businesses operate in an increasingly interconnected global environment, where geopolitical tensions, energy-market volatility, supply-chain disruptions, and shifting trade relationships can influence investment decisions and operating costs. For African economies, these pressures coexist with significant opportunities. The continent’s energy resources, critical minerals, expanding consumer markets and potential to develop local manufacturing and value chains position it to benefit from changes in global investment and supply-chain strategies. Realising this potential, however, will depend on infrastructure, reliable energy, skills, connectivity and predictable regulatory environments. Resilience moves to the centre of the growth agenda Cybersecurity and data security, alongside supply-chain resilience, are the leading threats to growth among African CEOs, each cited by 31% of respondents. The integration of AI into operating models and workflows follows at 27%. Investment priorities reflect the need to strengthen operational resilience. Some 45% of African CEOs are increasing investment in cybersecurity and digital-risk resilience, 36% in regulatory compliance and reporting, and 31% in AI integration. The findings suggest that resilience is no longer simply about protecting organisations against disruption. It is increasingly a condition for growth, enabling businesses to adapt to changing market conditions, protect critical operations and make investment decisions with greater confidence. For businesses operating across diverse African markets, this requires balancing immediate operational pressures with longer-term investment in infrastructure, technology, governance and capabilities. Tola Adeyemi, Senior Partner & CEO – KPMG One Africa, said: “African businesses are demonstrating confidence in their ability to grow, but the next phase of growth will require more than ambition. Leaders must make deliberate choices about where to invest, how to strengthen resilience and how to build organisations that can adapt to disruption. The opportunity is to translate the continent’s resources, markets and entrepreneurial capacity into more productive, competitive and sustainable businesses.” AI ambition is outpacing organisational readiness AI remains a strategic investment priority for African business leaders, with 72% of CEOs identifying it as a top investment priority, compared with 79% globally. Yet only 14% believe their organisations are moving at the right pace or ahead of AI developments, against 66% of global CEOs. This 52-percentage-point gap highlights a central challenge: African businesses recognise AI’s potential, but many are still working to develop the capabilities required to deploy it effectively and at scale. Expectations around returns also differ. While 48% of African CEOs expect AI investments to deliver returns within one to three years, compared with 71% globally, 42% expect returns after three years, against 12% globally. The longer investment horizon may reflect the work required to strengthen underlying data capabilities, integrate AI into existing systems, establish appropriate governance and develop the skills needed to realise value. It also reinforces the importance of evaluating AI against tangible business outcomes rather than adoption alone. The opportunity for African businesses is not simply to adopt new technology, but to use it to improve productivity, strengthen competitiveness and develop new products and services suited to local and regional markets. Workforce transformation becomes a growth imperative Technology investment is also reshaping workforce strategies. Despite the growing role of AI in business operations, 84% of African CEOs expect headcount to increase over the next three years, compared with 89% globally. At the same time, 86% intend to retain and retrain high-potential employees, 82% are redesigning roles, career paths and team structures for human-AI collaboration, and 74% are hiring AI and technology talent. Skills remain a significant constraint, with 59% identifying workforce skills gaps, 58% citing AI upskilling and training, and 52% pointing to challenges in attracting and retaining talent. These findings underline the relationship between technology adoption and workforce development. Businesses will need to invest in both if they are to translate digital ambition into productivity gains. For African economies, developing relevant skills and expanding access to technology capabilities will also be important to ensuring that digital transformation supports broader economic participation. Sustainability shifts towards measurable business value African CEOs are increasingly approaching sustainability through the lens of commercial performance, operational resilience and reporting readiness. Almost half, or 48%, report embedding sustainability more deeply into core business strategy, compared with 63% globally. Meanwhile, 40% are narrowing their focus to sustainability issues most critical to business performance, against 21% globally. Energy choices reflect the practical realities of operating across African markets. Some 41% of African CEOs prioritise energy demand optimisation, compared with 37% globally; 40% plan to diversify towards renewable or lower-carbon external energy supply, compared with 49% globally; and 15% plan to add dedicated generation or storage capacity, against 13% globally. Reporting readiness provides one of the clearest year-on-year indicators in the findings. The proportion of African CEOs who say their organisations have the capability to meet new sustainability reporting requirements has risen from 55% in the previous year to 65% in 2026. The improvement points to progress in organisational preparedness, although the broader challenge remains embedding sustainability into business decisions in ways that support resilience, efficiency and long-term value creation.

items.title: US stocks slide as Google parent's revenue miss revives AI spending jitters
items.description: US stock prices retreated on Thursday, with investors reassessing big tech’s massive AI spending spree as they digested high-profile earnings, crucial inflation data and the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision. All three major US stock indexes were in negative territory, with the Nasdaq dragged sharply lower by tech and tech-related megacaps in the wake of Alphabet’s disappointing quarterly results released late Wednesday. In contrast, the smallcap Russell 2000 advanced 0.8 per cent. Semiconductor stocks were poised to snap their four-day winning streak, dropping 2.0pc as investors sought to distinguish between companies that can fund their lofty AI ambitions from those that burn through cash and borrow funds to realise their ambitions. Alphabet was in the latter camp following its quarterly report released late on Wednesday. The Google parent’s revenue miss was compounded by its accelerated AI-related cash burn. Its shares slid 13.2pc. “A risk-off day like this, with small caps outperforming, is a good sign that thus far the market’s interpretation of cracks in the AI story doesn’t mean cracks in every corner of the market,” said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird in Louisville, Kentucky. “There’s plenty of other places to go with your money outside of the AI trade that have pretty decent prospects.” On Wednesday, Federal Reserve policymakers chose to hold US rates steady, acknowledging that while price pressures remain “elevated”, the central bank will decide on its next move as it “accumulates more information”. A raft of economic data released on Thursday answered that call, with a first take on third-quarter GDP that showed the US economy grew at a faster-than-expected pace in the third quarter, while price growth continued to gain heat with a war-related oil supply crunch feeding into broader, systemic inflation. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 315.36 points, or 0.59pc, to 52,163.07, the S&P 500 lost 48.73 points, or 0.63pc, to 7,695.25 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 441.15 points, or 1.66pc, to 26,108.35. Among the 11 major sectors in the S&P 500, communication services and tech were down the most, while healthcare led the gainers. Third-quarter earnings season has crossed the halfway point, with 253 of the companies in the S&P 500 having reported. Of those, 81pc have beaten analyst expectations, according to the most recent LSEG data. Analysts now expect aggregate third-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth of 31.0pc, year-on-year, per LSEG. Caterpillar topped quarterly profit estimates but left its growth targets unchanged. The heavy equipment maker’s shares tumbled 9.5pc. Eli Lilly jumped 6.3pc after the drugmaker lifted its revenue outlook on the strength of weight-loss drug sales. Ford gained 2.9pc following the automaker’s third-quarter revenue beat. Merck beat earnings expectations on the strength of its cancer drug Keytruda and its HPV vaccine Gardasil. The drugmaker’s shares advanced 4.4pc. Software stocks were broadly weak. Fortinet and ServiceNow dropped more than 20pc each after their quarterly results. Marvell Technology slumped 12.8pc after media reports said the company was in advanced talks to buy data-centre optics maker Lumentum Holdings. Lumentum shares rose 2.0pc. Amazon’s shares were off 3.9pc ahead of its earnings report, expected after the closing bell. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.59-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 113 new highs and 155 new lows on the NYSE. On the Nasdaq, 2,416 stocks rose and 2,221 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.09-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 19 new 52-week highs and six new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 81 new highs and 131 new lows.

items.title: MTN’s profit before tax for Q3 hits GH¢ 11.3 billion
items.description: Telecoms giant MTN has seen its profit before tax for the first nine months of this year hit GH¢ 11.3 billion. The figure represents a 51.8% jump over the GH¢ 7.7 billion it recorded during the same period in 2025. The figures were captured in MTN Ghana’s performance report for the nine-month period ended September 2026, released to the investing public on 29 October 2026. The report puts MTN’s total revenue as of September 30 at GH¢ 23.2 billion, representing a 35.7% increase over the figure recorded during the same period last year. In terms of expenditure, MTN invested some GH¢ 3.2 billion in capital expenditure during the first nine months of this year. Service revenue increased by 33.5% YoY to GH¢ 23.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, reflecting what MTN describes as continued execution across both our Connectivity and Fintech businesses. Sustained demand for data services, increasing adoption of digital financial services, and continued customer engagement across our digital platforms supported growth. Mobile Money Business MTN’s Mobile Money Business grew by 26.5% to reach GH¢ 5.3 billion, according to the company. The growth was supported by continued expansion across both core wallet services and advanced financial services, alongside a 6.9% YoY increase in active Mobile Money users to 18.9 million. Basic services revenue increased by 22.2% YoY to GH¢ 3.5 billion, supported by growth in person-to-person transfers, while advanced services revenue increased by 28.7% YoY to GH¢ 1.9 billion, driven by higher adoption of digital payments, lending, and other value-added services. Transaction volumes and values continued to grow during the period, reflecting broader ecosystem participation and increasing digital payment adoption. Mobile Money contributed 23.2% of service revenue, compared with 24.9% in the corresponding period of 2025. MTN puts the number of active Mobile Money users at 18.9 million, representing a 6.9% increase. CEO on Third Quarter Earnings According to MTN Ghana Chief Executive Officer Stephen Blewett, growth remained well diversified across the company’s key revenue streams. He also stated that data revenue increased by 39.9% YoY in Q3, supported by sustained demand for data and digital services. The Chief Executive Officer said the third-quarter performance further strengthened the company’s nine-month results, demonstrating the resilience and diversification of its growth engines. He added that “this performance also reinforced our capacity to generate earnings and cash flow while continuing to invest in the long-term growth of the business and deliver returns to shareholders.” Mr. Blewett added that, while the global environment remains challenging, Ghana’s operating environment remains relatively stable. This is due to the fact that “inflation remains on a moderating trajectory, external reserves have strengthened, and economic activity continues to demonstrate resilience.” Dividend Payment Based on its financial performance for the third quarter, the MTN Board is proposing a gross interim dividend of GH¢ 0.03 per share for the third quarter ending 30 September 2026. The company stated that all dividends are subject to the deduction of applicable taxes. The number of ordinary shares in issue as of the date of the declaration is 13,236,175,050. Scancom PLC’s tax reference number is C0003632776. MTN said the declaration is in line with the requirements of Ghana Stock Exchange rules, including the relevant dates relating to the payment of the dividend. Consequently, an investor purchasing MTN GH shares before the relevant date will be entitled to the Q3 interim dividend. However, an investor buying MTN GH shares on or after Thursday, 26 November 2026, will not be entitled to the Q3 interim dividend. On Thursday, 10 December 2026, the net dividend will be transferred electronically to the bank accounts or mobile money wallets of shareholders who use these facilities.

items.title: Tourisme saharien : spectacle inédit de montgolfières dans le ciel de Timimoun
items.description: Timimoun , l’Oasis rouge, a vécu ce jeudi au rythme des montgolfières qui ont survolé les dunes. Une foule nombreuse constituée d’habitants locaux et de touristes a assisté à cet événement inédit dans la région. La ville abrite depuis hier mercredi et jusqu’au 31 octobre prochain la 1re édition du Festival international de montgolfières et des cerfs-volants géants, organisé par Algeria Balloon Festival, sous le haut patronage du wali de Timimoun et en collaboration avec l’agence d’événementiel Riah w Taslia. La journée d’hier a vu l’arrivée de participants, dont une vingtaine d’étrangers. L’inauguration de cet événement a été marquée par la présentation de la montgolfière aux couleurs du drapeau algérien. Timimoun renforce son attractivité touristique avec le festival de montgolfières Le programme prévoit pour demain vendredi l’organisation d’un concours de cerfs-volants géants, en plus des vols de montgolfières. D’autres activités musicales et folkloriques sont programmées par les organisateurs de ce festival qui a drainé de nombreux touristes nationaux et étrangers. Timimoun est l’une des destinations phares du tourisme saharien en Algérie, aux côtés de Ghardaïa, Taghit, Djanet et du Hoggar-Tassili. L’Oasis rouge est notamment connue pour ses foggaras et son vieux ksar. Timimoun est réputée aussi pour l’Ahellil, chant poétique religieux classé par l’Unesco comme patrimoine immatériel de l’humanité. Le festival de l’Ahellil qui se tient à la fin de décembre de chaque année attire également de nombreux touristes. Surnommé l’Oasis rouge en raison de la couleur de ses constructions en terre cuite, Timimoun a enregistré plus de 4 500 touristes étrangers et quelque 30 000 visiteurs nationaux, durant la saison 2024/2025. items.title: 'Not related to defence': Govt responds to Fazl's remarks about Makkah pact countries' meeting in Tehran
items.description: Federal ministers on Thursday responded to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s remarks regarding a recent huddle in Tehran comprising the Makkah defence pact countries and Iran. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the meeting was not related to defence. Hence, Asif said his presence was not required, while Naqvi explained the reasons for his participation. The remarks came after the JUI-F chief questioned Asif’s absence and Naqvi’s presence at the meeting. The meeting brought together top officials from Iran and member countries of the Makkah Defence Alliance — including Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin. On Iran’s side, President Masoud Pezeshkian, Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi were present. The huddle agreed to “continue their dialogue to bolster cooperation among the four regional nations, including in the areas of regional peace and security”. On Wednesday, Fazl referred to the development during his address in the National Assembly (NA) and commented: “A defence pact is taking shape in Iran, a meeting is under way (there), and the defence minister is sitting here.” Amid laughter and desk thumping in the Lower House, he referred to Naqvi’s presence at the Tehran huddle and questioned: “The interior minister is required there as well?” Then, taking a jibe at Asif, he repeated the defence minister’s phrase that he had used against the PTI. “There is your respect and stature — koi sharam hoti hai, koi haya hoti hai (have some shame, show some modesty),” he said, breaking into laughter. Responding to him in the NA on Thursday, Asif said no defence pact was taking shape in Tehran, nor was the discussion focused on Pakistan’s defence or any related matter. He said CDF Munir had “assumed a role for Pakistan” following last year’s military conflict with India. That role, he said, was of “peace and dialogue so that peace is established in our region”. Since then, he noted, Pakistan has signed two defence pacts — the Makkah defence pact and the Badr Memorandum of Understanding. “I was involved in those pacts as I am the defence minister,” he explained, adding that the meeting in Tehran was “not the defence ministry’s mandate”. The CDF had gone there “as a messenger of peace and paved the ground” for the huddle, he said, ostensibly referring to Tehran last week. During that visit, the CDF had proposed the Tehran meeting, according to Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei. Asif said this was the situation and he was “not needed in Tehran”. He added that the CDF had played a role in averting a confrontation. “The situation could have deteriorated as far as the Yemen issue is concerned […] There has been some talk and peace may emerge in the coming days or week as far as Saudi Arabia versus Yemen [sic] is concerned.” Asif advised Fazl to be the bigger person and said his criticism was “misplaced”. The defence minister further said Pakistan’s and the CDF’s role at the international level should be acknowledged, keeping political differences aside. He said one should at least show some dignity. ‘Not related to defence’ Meanwhile, in the Senate, Naqvi also responded to Fazl’s remarks on his participation in the Tehran meeting. The proceedings were marred by loud exchanges between the interior minister and JUI-F Senator Kamran Murtaza. Naqvi clarified that he and CDF Munir undertook the visit to “handle the ongoing crisis in Iran”. On Fazl’s query of why Asif had not gone there, he said, “He (Fazl) did not know that this [trip] was not related to defence.” Defending his inclusion, the minister said: “I do not go out of my own volition. I have been especially tasked by the prime minister sahib ; he has entrusted me with some matters regarding the current crisis of the [Iran] war, because of which I go.” The independent senator noted that the JUI-F had been commenting on him for many days. “I personally had heartfelt respect for Maulana Fazlur Rehman, but yesterday when he said I spit on the state, that respect ended,” Naqvi said. Naqvi said he wanted to ask Fazl and his party’s senators present there just one question and then noted that JUI-F leaders had made very “disgusting statements about institutions” three to four months ago. This prompted Senator Murtaza to object, saying he could not speak on a personal agenda in the House. Presiding Officer Shahadat Awan also immediately said he was expunging the word “disgusting” from Naqvi’s remarks. As Murtaza continued shouting, Naqvi said, “You should listen here … You will have to listen.” The presiding officer noted that Naqvi was a member of the Senate and urged the JUI-F leader to take his seat. Resuming his remarks, Naqvi said, “Giving people the perception that this was a defence pact; this was not a defence agreement at all. He added: “For them, the state is like a mother until the day they can squeeze it dry. The state is very good as long as they can extract wealth from the state, and when you do not get a share in the state and the government, then you spit on the state. This is not appropriate anywhere.” Murtaza again interrupted, objecting to Naqvi’s language, at which the latter replied that the other side had also used similar language a day ago. As the JUI-F senator continued speaking amid the presiding officer’s calls to halt cross-talk, Naqvi said, “If they criticise, they should garner and keep the courage to take the answer as well. This is no way [to behave] that you go and say whatever you want.” The interior minister then went on to criticise the JUI-F, alleging that it “used Islam for business and for politics”. Amid the ruckus, PML-N’s Abid Sher Ali also stood up and responded loudly, prompting State Minister of Interior Tallal Chaudhry and the presiding officer to urge him to take his seat. Naqvi then addressed PTI’s Ali Zafar and said, “These very people (JUI-F) used to come to us before governor’s rule [was imposed] and say, ‘Impose governor’s rule, rid us of them!’ […] Those who come and sit with you and engage in opposition wanted governor’s rule imposed from their hearts. I will prove this to you.” Addressing JUI-F, the interior minister said, “Now, you will not get jobs in the state. Now you will not get money from the state, nor will you get tickets from the state.” He asserted that it was the JUI-F that was “continuously crossing the line” and that they would get a response if they kept doing so. ‘Full of contradictions’ In his remarks in the NA, Asif alleged that Fazl’s past “is full of contradictions”. “You taunt me with ‘have some shame, show some modesty’, but you should also have some shame and show some modesty. How many perks have you enjoyed over the past 40 years? You have been violating the very principles that you have been highlighting,” the PML-N leader said. He recalled that Fazl had also offered to mediate with Kabul. “Were you the foreign minister?” he questioned, alleging that the move was aimed at “value addition to his politics and leverage that to extract maximum advantage from the government”. Asif said Fazl had been in the government with every political party, making an incomplete remark: “When you don’t get a share in the power —” “When you delete the past from your memory and attack your rivals — at least I don’t have that courage. When I speak, my past is fresh in my mind; that if I say this, whether I would be taunted that we supported General Ziaul Haq’s government,” he went on to say. The defence minister recalled that Fazl was part of the Musharraf government, had also been an opposition leader in the House and also served as the Kashmir Committee chairperson. He said a person serving as the head of such a committee that raises issues at an international forum should have “impeccable credentials”. When some lawmakers opposed him in favour of Fazl, he remarked, “The Maulana now needs women’s support. He is unable to find a man.” He also accused Fazl of “targeting our diplomatic efforts”, saying that the government’s achievement at the global stage had not received the commendation they deserved. Asif said his advice to the JUI-F would be a line often seen on buses and trucks: “ Mehnat kar, hasad na kar (work hard and don’t envy).” He ended his address, alleging that had Fazl been given some share in the governance in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province, the JUI-F chief’s address the previous day would not have been delivered. “This sideshow that they (JUI-F) are running, I feel that it is unfortunate that our sisters have been forced to defend the men [of JUI-F] while the men are nowhere to be seen,” Asif remarked. Describing Fazl’s address as “blackmail”, Asif warned against coming into power based on “compromises”. “Sitting in the opposition would be a more respectable approach, rather than sitting with people who will blackmail you,” he said. “We as senior parliamentarians should convey to the nation that we will not do group-based politics but politics rooted in the constitution and [..] for the security of the country,” Asif urged, adding that lawmakers should chart a way forward together, rather than “grabbing each other by the collar”. JUI-F’s Murtaza alleges ‘programme to sling mud’ at Fazl In remarks after the Senate ruckus, JUI-F’s Murtaza accused the government of staging a “requested programme”. “I think nizam sahib (Mr System) sent messages and made calls to many people today, and told them to sling mud at Maulana sahib like this,” he said on Geo News ’ programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Sath’, apparently referring to Naqvi. Murtaza questioned why Asif “suddenly remembered” to respond to Fazl the next day, rather than using his right of reply “even though he was present” in the NA yesterday. He went on to object to the interior minister making “personal accusations”, even though he could have simply explained that the prime minister had tasked him with peace efforts. The JUI-F senator insisted that Fazl’s remarks were not particularly about Pakistan but “if a state starts making its children fight each other”, asking if the ministers were considering that the state was doing so. Asked what Fazl implied, Murtaza maintained that the JUI-F’s stance was “about every such state” that engaged in such acts. The senator also claimed that Chaudhry had approached him with an “offer for a certain thing” when he was in the Senate hall. “Did I reject you or not? 26th Amendment,” Murtaza said, with Chaudhry acknowledging that a “lot of things were being discussed at the time of 26th Amendment” but “not everything should be disclosed”. Meanwhile, appearing on the same show, the state minister for interior regretted that Fazl, despite being a senior politician and a religious leader, “made martyrs a point of his and discuss it to advance his politics”. Chaudhry said he had noted immense anger and frustration visible in the JUI-F chief’s demeanour in recent days. Asked if the government wanted a “clash” with the JUI-F chief, the PML-N leader said, “I think Maulana sahib is deliberately clashing and bringing up such issues, after which no option is left for us other than to respond to it. Today, I have never seen Kamran Murtaza sahib in such a state of anger in my entire life.” He highlighted that Fazl had questioned “what has this state given us”. “Do you think the state has given you nothing?” he asked. Electoral reforms committee In his remarks, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas claimed KP had been “snatched from the people” and reiterated the opposition’s allegations of rigging in the 2024 general elections. “If even one person’s vote is snatched, it is a crime. It is the responsibility of those conducting elections to protect the vote. Earlier also you laid a crooked brick, and Pakistan broke. On Feb 8, elections were stolen. While stealing elections, where have you reached — you have even stolen Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” he claimed. The opposition leader said no society could progress without law, or function if law existed but without its implementation. The House also took up a motion moved by Minister of State for Law Barrister Aqeel Malik for the constitution of a parliamentary electoral reforms committee. PTI’s Zafar said he could write down entire electoral reforms on paper in an hour. “The issue is implementation. Make such a committee and procedure that the electoral process is actually implemented. Whatever they want to do, only that is approved,” he said. Barrister Aqeel said the issue could be resolved by sitting together and asked members to bring their proposals.

items.title: Germany’s Zverev becomes tennis world No. 1
items.description: Alexander Zverev accelerated his ascension to number one in the world rankings for the first time in his career on Thursday as he beat Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 to reach the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open. The 29-year-old German was already assured of finishing the season top of the ATP rankings but, in the absence of current incumbent Jannik Sinner, two-time Grand Slam champion Zverev will now take that crown in next week’s updated standings after winning his opening two matches in the Austrian capital. Long seen as tennis’ nearly-man, Zverev has enjoyed a stellar 2026, breaking his major duck by picking up the titles at the French and US Opens. Now he has broken further ground by becoming only the 30th man to claim top spot since the rankings were first published in 1973. He will be aged 29 years and 196 days when Monday’s new rankings are published, making him the second-oldest first-time number one after Australian John Newcombe. Due to a knee injury Italy’s Sinner decided to end his season at the start of October, opening the way for Zverev to dethrone him. And the big-serving Hamburg native ensured he did just that ahead of the season-ending ATP Finals next month by seeing off Martin Landaluce and Griekspoor in his opening two matches in Vienna. Zverev needed to save four match points against Spain’s Landaluce in his first-round match on Tuesday, but was much more comfortable as he defeated Griekspoor in straight sets to write his name into the history books. He raced out of the blocks on Thursday, breaking the 30-year-old Dutchman in the very first game and then confidently serving his way into a one-set lead. The second frame went to 5-5 before Zverev pounced on Griekspoor’s serve to get his nose in front. The match met an unexpected stoppage as Zverev brought up match point when a smash off the German’s racquet caused part of the electronic board behind Griekspoor to malfunction. But once the umpire covered the problematic panel up with a towel, Zverev then sealed his new ranking with an unreturnable serve. items.title: Djignaky : le plan de développement communal de 10 milliards de FCFA validé
items.description: Le Conseil municipal de la commune de Djinaky a adopté, vendredi 23 octobre, son Plan de développement communal (PDC) 2026-2030 aligné au référentiel « Vision Sénégal 2050 ». Il est organisé autour de quatre axes stratégiques déclinés en programmes et projets. Le coût global du Pdc est estimé à plus de 10 milliards de FCFA. BIGNONA – « Bâtir un pôle rural prospère, inclusif et résilient ». Telle est la vision de la commune de Djinaky dirigée par Alphoussény Diémé qui compte s’appuyer sur une gouvernance participative et la valorisation des ressources naturelles. L’équipe municipale entend matérialiser cette vision à travers un Plan de développement communal (PDC) 2026-2030, validé vendredi 23 octobre. Dans les projets, il s’agira, d’après le maire, de transformer les atouts territoriaux en facteurs de développement et de création de richesses, de valoriser le dividende démographique et de développer un système d’exploitation et de gestion durable de l’espace communal, résilient au changement et au dérèglement climatiques. Le coût global de financement du Pdc est estimé à 10 218 050 000 FCFA. Pour sa réalisation, la municipalité compte sur le budget communal alimenté par les produits des taxes, les transferts de l'État, les financements de divers organismes nationaux qui travaillent dans la décentralisation comme le Programme d'appui aux communes et agglomérations du Sénégal (Pacasen), la coopération décentralisée ainsi que sur les projets/programmes de l'État (Anrac, Plan Diomaye pour la Casamance…), mais également sur les emprunts et le partenariat public-privé. Alphoussény Diémé a expliqué que la mise en œuvre de cet outil de gestion communale, dont l’élaboration est financée par le Programme de développement économique de la Casamance (PDEC), avec l’accompagnement de l’ARD de Ziguinchor, sera précédée d’une large concertation à l’issue de laquelle les meilleurs schémas organisationnels seront construits pour garantir son succès dans tous les domaines de compétences transférées, essentiellement. Aussi, pense le maire, « la vocation agricole de la commune, en cohérence avec celle du pôle territoire sud, invite à renforcer la collaboration avec les organisations paysannes ». Riche commune Située dans l’arrondissement de Kataba 1, la commune de Djinaky couvre une superficie d’environ 446,58 km² et compte 25 villages. Elle est limitée au nord par Kataba 1, au sud par Diégoune et Kartiack, à l’ouest par la commune de Kafountine et à l’est par les communes de Suelle et Djibidione. À en croire le maire, la circonscription abrite d’importantes formations végétales et plusieurs espèces fauniques. « Les formations forestières couvrent une superficie de 21 812,56 ha, soit 48,85 % de la superficie communale », fait-il savoir. Il poursuit : « Riches et variées, elles sont composées de la végétation dense, de la savane boisée et de la mangrove et sont exploitées par les populations qui y prélèvent des produits ligneux (bois de chauffe, bois d’œuvre), non ligneux (fruits, feuilles, racines, écorces) et de la pharmacopée, avec des revenus pour la population et une alimentation en protéines végétales. A lire aussi : « Le Soleil » et la commune de Djinaky signent un partenariat Cependant, dénonce Alphoussény Diémé, la forêt et les mangroves font face à plusieurs menaces. « Il s’agit, entre autres, de l’exploitation abusive et des coupes illicites des forêts, des feux de brousse, du déficit pluviométrique et de la disparition de certaines espèces animales », liste-t-il. Les jeunes représentent 75 % de la population de la commune. À l’instar de plusieurs communes du département de Bignona, « Djinaky n’a pas été épargnée par la crise casamançaise, qui a occasionné des déplacements de populations abandonnant leurs villages », explique le maire. À la faveur de l’accalmie notée depuis quelques années, informe-t-il, ces populations déplacées ont entamé leur réinstallation progressive avec l’accompagnement des ONG, des partenaires au développement et des projets et programmes de l’État, notamment le « Plan Diomaye pour la Casamance ». Le maraîchage, activité phare dans la commune Le maraîchage, ajoute Alphoussény Diémé, est une activité phare des jeunes et des femmes de la commune. Elle se développe dans des blocs maraîchers collectifs, notamment des groupements de femmes organisées sous forme de GIE, avec l’appui des partenaires techniques et financiers. Il y a aussi des blocs maraîchers individuels. « Le maraîchage participe à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des ménages grâce à la commercialisation des productions », confie le maire. L’existence d’équipements de transformation participe également à l’allègement des travaux de la femme et favorise l’entrepreneuriat féminin. À ce titre, il est dénombré 31 moulins, 19 décortiqueuses, 12 batteuses, 4 presses à huile et 3 unités de transformation, dont 2 privées (l’une étant non fonctionnelle). Kadidiatou SONKO (Correspondante)

items.title: 5th Edition of Ghana Corporate Brands Conference and Honours launched
items.description: Maven Communications is set to bring together C-suite executives, brand and marketing leaders, communications practitioners, customer experience professionals, academics and policymakers for the fifth edition of the Ghana Corporate Brands Conference and Honours, a platform focused on the future of branding in Ghana’s evolving business environment. Under the theme, “Shaping the Future of Corporate Branding in Ghana: Building Brands with Strategic Intent, Inspiring Excellence, and Earning Lasting Trust”, the event is expected to convene key voices from business, academia and industry to discuss emerging branding trends, reputation management, customer expectations and the growing role of technology in shaping public perception. The conference comes at a time when organisations face increasing pressure to strengthen stakeholder trust, differentiate themselves in competitive markets and remain relevant in an era defined by digital influence and instant access to information. Responding to a changing branding landscape Ghanaian consumers are widely perceived to have a preference for foreign goods and services, a perception rooted in the country’s early exposure to international trade, when merchant vessels arriving on the shores of the then Gold Coast introduced local consumers to foreign products. Today, however, the marketplace has become significantly more complex. Consumers are better informed, more connected and more influential than ever before. Through digital platforms and social media, they can compare brands, evaluate customer experiences and make purchasing decisions based on information from virtually anywhere in the world. For organisations operating in Ghana, this presents both a challenge and an opportunity. While competition extends far beyond national borders, businesses also have greater opportunities to build brands that inspire confidence, foster loyalty and create lasting value. Against this backdrop, the Ghana Corporate Brands Conference and Honours seeks to stimulate meaningful conversations around brand leadership, reputation management and sustainable business growth. Brand building beyond products and services Speaking on behalf of Maven Communications, Managing Director and Event Director Seth (Jojo) Danso Asante said successful brands are now defined by far more than the products and services they offer. “The business landscape is evolving rapidly. Brands are no longer defined solely by their products or services. Brand perception, customer expectations, digital influence, reputation and commercial performance are increasingly interconnected,” he said. “Changing consumer behaviour, rapid technological advancement, social media, artificial intelligence, digital journalism and greater access to information have fundamentally changed how organisations build brands.” According to him, organisations must adopt a more deliberate and integrated approach to brand management to remain competitive and credible in today’s marketplace. From reputation management to reputation leadership As stakeholder expectations continue to evolve, reputation is increasingly becoming a leadership issue rather than a function handled exclusively by communications or public relations teams. Every customer interaction, employee experience, leadership decision, digital engagement and public statement contributes to how an organisation is perceived. Industry leaders increasingly recognise that brands are ultimately judged by the experiences they create, the promises they fulfil, the trust they earn and the value they deliver. The conference will therefore examine the intersection of brand strategy, marketing, communications, customer experience, reputation management and business performance, offering practical insights into building brands that are resilient, distinctive and commercially sustainable. Honouring excellence in corporate and product branding Running alongside the conference is the Ghana Corporate Brands Honours, an initiative established to recognise organisations and individuals that have demonstrated a sustained commitment to building, managing and strengthening corporate and product brands. The honours will celebrate excellence in areas such as corporate identity, product positioning, market visibility, brand consistency, consumer engagement and strategic brand development. Recognition through the honours provides a benchmark of achievement and highlights institutions whose branding efforts continue to contribute to the growth and advancement of Ghana’s corporate landscape.

items.title: NAIMOS targets suppliers of equipment used in illegal mining in Aowin and Enchi
items.description: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has announced plans to target individuals and businesses manufacturing or selling equipment used in illegal mining as part of efforts to curb galamsey in Aowin and Enchi in the Western North Region. Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel S. K. Appiah, said the taskforce would focus on the supply chain supporting illegal mining activities in addition to enforcement against operators. Speaking during a tour of the taskforce’s operations in the area, he said the objective was to enforce the law and halt the destruction of the environment without unnecessarily undermining legitimate livelihoods. “We are not here to destroy livelihoods, but to enforce the law,” he said. “A lot of people have gone out of their way, destroying water, destroying forest reserves.” Aowin and Enchi are endowed with gold deposits, forest reserves and major water bodies, including the Tano and Bia rivers. However, illegal mining activities have raised concerns about damage to water bodies, agricultural lands and forest ecosystems. Colonel Appiah warned that continued environmental degradation could have serious consequences for future generations, urging residents to support efforts to stop illegal mining. “I always tell them that if their predecessors had done it this way, we’d not have been alive to meet it as it is. And we count on your support to ensure that we are able to curb illegal mining within this district,” he said. He expressed confidence that sustained enforcement and community cooperation could help restore areas damaged by illegal mining. “So that going into the future we’ll be able to recover the lands, recover the water, and then we’ll see marked improvement in the levels,” he added. The planned crackdown extends the focus beyond miners to businesses and individuals who manufacture, distribute or sell equipment used in illegal operations. NAIMOS is expected to continue its activities in the Western North Region, targeting those involved in illegal mining and the supply networks that support it. Illegal mining, commonly known as galamsey, remains a major environmental concern in Ghana because of its effects on forests, rivers and farmland. Although successive governments have pledged to tackle the practice, enforcement and accountability remain central to efforts to address the problem. The effectiveness of the latest operation will depend on the extent to which authorities can enforce the law consistently and disrupt the networks sustaining illegal mining.

items.title: Awujale succession: DSS invites Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Department of State Services (DSS) in Ogun State has reportedly invited three leaders of the Fusengbuwa ruling house over the alleged sale of expression-of-interest forms to princes seeking to become the next Awujale of Ijebuland. Those reportedly invited are the Chairman of the ruling house, Otunba Abdulateef Owoyemi; the deputy chairman, Otunba Dokun Ajidagba; and the vice chairman, Prof. Fassy Yusuf. The invitation comes amid an ongoing dispute over the selection of a new Awujale following the death of the previous monarch, Oba Sikiru Adetona, in July 2025, at the age of 91, after 65 years on the throne. A letter circulating online, purportedly signed by one Yemi Oloto, directed the three ruling house leaders to appear before the State Director of Security at the DSS office in Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta, on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 4 p.m. The letter, which indicated that the meeting was connected with an investigation into the sale of expression-of-interest forms to princes interested in the vacant stool, read in part: “I am directed to invite you for a meeting with the State Director of Security (SDS), Department of State Services (DSS), Ogun State, Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta, today, 29th October, 2026, 1600 hours (4 p.m.). “The meeting is in furtherance of investigating activities in respect of the sale of expression-of-interest forms to interested princes for the vacant stool of Awujale of Ijebuland.” The letter further stated that an officer had been designated at the main gate to facilitate the invitees’ entry into the premises, before concluding with the director’s best wishes. When contacted, Prof. Yusuf confirmed receiving the invitation but said he was in Abuja attending to a matter before the Supreme Court and would therefore be unable to honour it. The professor of Mass Communication and lawyer said: “I just received the letter from the DSS not long ago, but I am in Abuja attending to a matter at the Supreme Court. I have discountenanced their letter.” Similarly, Ajidagba confirmed receiving the invitation on Thursday afternoon, saying it was delivered at about 2:30 p.m. with instructions to report at the DSS office by 4:30 p.m. He, however, questioned the timing of the invitation, arguing that matters relating to the succession process were already before the courts. “I received the DSS invitation on Thursday at about 2:30 p.m., and I was told to report at their office by 4:30 p.m. There was, however, no way I could honour such an invitation when all of these matters are already in court. The status quo must be allowed to remain; that is the position of the law,” he said. There was no immediate confirmation from the DSS on the reported invitations or the allegations prompting them. The latest development comes against the backdrop of previous engagements between security agencies and stakeholders in the Awujale succession process. Security agencies, including the Ogun State Police Command, had reportedly summoned nine kingmakers in Ijebu-Ode and the three Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders on two occasions to appear at the police headquarters in Eleweran, Abeokuta. The invitations were said to be connected with allegations of bribery and financial inducement in the selection of a new Awujale and paramount ruler of Ijebuland. Owoyemi has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in connection with the succession process. The three ruling house leaders have also instituted legal proceedings against the Ogun State government over the suspension of the selection process, which has remained stalled since January 2026. In August, the Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders approached the Ogun State High Court sitting in Ijebu-Ode, seeking orders compelling the completion of the process for selecting the next Awujale and paramount ruler of Ijebuland. The suit, numbered HCJ/149/2026 and dated August 21, 2026, was instituted by Owoyemi, Ajidagba and Yusuf. The defendants include Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun; the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Mr Oluwasina Ogungbade (SAN); the Ogun State Executive Council; the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Ganiyu Hamzat; and the Secretary of Ijebu-Ode Local Government. Also joined as defendants are members of the Awujale Afobaje/Kingmakers Council, including Olorogun Sonny Kuku, Chief Rasheed Adesanya, Chief Oluwaranti Lekan Osifeso, Chief Jimi Lawal, Chief Abimbola Okenla, Chief Kunle Ogunade, Chief Agboola Alausa, Chief Adebisi Adaran and Chief Ayotunde Ola Odulaja. Among other reliefs, the claimants are asking the court to determine whether the state government had the legal authority to order or facilitate the alleged entry into and locking of the Awujale palace on January 20, 2026. According to the claimants, the action was intended to physically prevent the kingmakers from convening and concluding the statutory process for selecting a successor to the late monarch. The dispute has further complicated efforts to fill the vacant traditional stool, with the government maintaining that the process must be conducted peacefully and in accordance with the applicable procedures. Meanwhile, Governor Abiodun has assured the people of Ijebuland that a new Awujale will emerge before May 29, 2027. The governor gave the assurance on Tuesday at the Ogun East Senatorial District stakeholders’ meeting in Ijebu-Ode, where he engaged representatives of various interest groups on traditional affairs, governance and the economic prospects of the district. According to a statement issued on Wednesday, Abiodun reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to ensuring a smooth and acceptable succession process. “On the succession process for the revered Awujale stool, Abiodun assured the people that his administration was committed to facilitating a smooth, peaceful and widely acceptable process leading to the emergence of a new monarch,” the statement said. The governor acknowledged the significance of the Awujale institution to the cultural heritage, identity and unity of Ijebuland, urging residents to remain calm and patient while the necessary procedures were being concluded. He added that his administration was giving the matter the attention it deserved to ensure that the process was completed peacefully and that the eventual emergence of a new monarch enjoyed the acceptance and support of the people. The Awujale stool became vacant in July 2025 following the death of Oba Adetona, who ruled for 65 years and was widely regarded as one of Nigeria’s longest-reigning traditional rulers. The Ogun State Government halted the succession process in January 2026, citing petitions from security agencies and other stakeholders. The suspension followed an earlier halt in December 2025 over procedural concerns. A total of 95 aspirants—94 princes and one princess—reportedly emerged from the Fusengbuwa ruling house nomination exercise held in Ijebu-Ode in December 2025 before the government suspended further proceedings. items.title: JOJ DAKAR 2026 : plus de 2 milliards F CFA d’équipements sportifs dans 5 communes de Dakar
items.description: En vue des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ Dakar 2026), Moussa Bala Fofana, ministre de l’Urbanisme, des Collectivités territoriales et de l’Aménagement du territoire, a inauguré, jeudi, à Keur Massar de nouvelles infrastructures sportives d'une valeur de plus de deux milliards de FCFA. De Keur Massar Nord à Keur Massar Sud en passant par Sangalkam, Dalifort et Médina Gounass, ces équipements modernes permettront à la jeunesse locale d'être au plus près de la ferveur de Dakar 2026. Dans le cadre des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ Dakar 2026), l’Agence de développement municipal (ADM) a procédé, jeudi, à Keur Massar, à l'inauguration des infrastructures et équipements sportifs de proximité. Présidée par Moussa Bala Fofana, ministre de l’Urbanisme, des Collectivités territoriales et de l’Aménagement du territoire, l’inauguration des équipements sportifs s’inscrit aussi dans la mise en œuvre du Progep 2. Ainsi, elle marque une étape décisive dans l’aménagement territorial et la préparation des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse (JOJ Dakar 2026). D’un coût global de plus de 2 milliards F CFA, les réalisations de ce projet couvrent 5 communes cibles, notamment Dalifort, Medina Gounass, Keur Massar Nord, Keur Massar Sud et Sangalkam. Dans le cadre de ce projet, 6 terrains de football à gazon synthétique, 2 terrains multifonctionnels, des parcours sportifs de proximité et des aménagements paysagers attractifs et innovants ont été réalisés. Dans cette dynamique, l’Adm entend territorialiser les Joj, faire émerger un sport de masse inclusif tout en posant les bases de la détection et de l’accompagnement de l’élite sportive nationale. « Au-delà de la pierre et du gazon, ce que nous inaugurons aujourd'hui est un choix politique et social majeur. Celui de replacer les territoires, les communautés et, surtout, la jeunesse au cœur de l'action publique. Ces espaces ne seront pas de simples terrains de jeu. Ils seront des lieux de pratique sportive, certes, mais aussi des espaces de rencontre, d'apprentissage, de solidarité et d'épanouissement collectif », a déclaré Moussa Bala Fofana, ministre de l’Urbanisme, des Collectivités territoriales et de l’Aménagement des territoires. D’après le ministre, l’inauguration de ces infrastructures traduit, d’une part, la volonté de l’État de faire des investissements publics des réalisations directement utiles à nos concitoyens. D’autre part, a ajouté M. Fofana, cette initiative met en lumière l’ambition de faire des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse Dakar 2026 un accélérateur de transformation urbaine et sociale, dont les bénéfices doivent perdurer bien après la clôture des compétitions. A lire aussi : Baseball 5: huit Lionceaux pour un défi historique En outre, selon lui, le sport occupe une place centrale dans la vision de transformation portée par l’Agenda national de transformation Sénégal 2050. À ses yeux, le sport est à la fois un facteur de santé et de bien-être, une école de discipline et de persévérance, un puissant vecteur de cohésion sociale et un véritable levier de développement économique. « Les Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse Dakar 2026 offrent au Sénégal et à l’Afrique une occasion historique. Ils témoignent de notre capacité à accueillir le monde et à faire rayonner notre pays. La devise des Jeux, « L’Afrique accueille, Dakar célèbre », fait écho à l’hospitalité sénégalaise et à cette Teranga qui nous rassemble et que nous souhaitons partager avec le monde entier. Mais la réussite des JOJ ne se mesurera pas uniquement à la qualité de l’organisation, aux performances des athlètes ou à la visibilité internationale de notre pays », a-t-il dit. Pour lui, le résultat va se mesurer sur ce qui restera dans nos communes et nos quartiers en termes d’équipements accessibles, des espaces publics mieux aménagés, des communautés mobilisées et une jeunesse qui pourra continuer à pratiquer, à se rencontrer et à s’engager. Bada MBATHIE

items.title: Sénatoriales du 20 décembre : prorogation de la date de dépôt des candidatures (DGE)
items.description: La Direction Générale des Élections (DGE) accorde un délai supplémentaire aux candidats aux élections sénatoriales prévues le 20 décembre 2026. Initialement fixée au jeudi 29 octobre, la date limite de dépôt des dossiers est désormais reportée au samedi 31 octobre à 20 heures . Dans son communiqué, l’institution électorale informe les citoyens et les acteurs politiques de cette modification du calendrier de réception des candidatures. Le document précise : « La Direction Générale des Élections – DGE informe l'ensemble des citoyens et des acteurs politiques que la date limite de dépôt des candidatures aux élections sénatoriales, initialement fixée au jeudi 29 octobre 2026, est prorogée jusqu'au samedi 31 octobre 2026 à 20h00. » Ce report offre ainsi deux jours supplémentaires aux candidats pour finaliser et soumettre leurs dossiers. La DGE rappelle toutefois que le respect de cette nouvelle échéance est impératif : aucun dossier ne sera accepté après le samedi 31 octobre 2026 à 20 heures.

items.title: We’re satisfied with Afenyo-Markin’s leadership in Parliament; rules out changes to Minority leadership – NPP
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) says it is satisfied with the work of the Minority leadership in Parliament under Alexander Afenyo-Markin and has no plans to replace him. The party’s General Secretary, Justin Kodua Frimpong, said the party had not considered any change in the leadership, dismissing reports circulating on a flyer that another MP had been selected to take over as Minority Leader. Speaking at a media briefing on Thursday, October 29, he said the party’s leadership was happy with the work of the Minority Caucus and would continue to support it. “The party has never thought about even deliberating to change the leadership in Parliament. We have not,” he said. He accused those spreading the reports of attempting to create confusion within the party’s parliamentary caucus and urged the public to disregard the claims. “Those who are busily peddling lies and trying to create chaos or confusion among the leadership in Parliament and the mighty Minority Caucus, they will not succeed,” he said. Mr Kodua said the party’s elected officers were “overwhelmingly satisfied” with the work of the leadership led by Mr Afenyo-Markin. “We are happy with the work they are doing in Parliament and we shall continue to support them. There is no meeting, there is no attempt to change the leadership in Parliament,” he added. He said the party’s support for the Minority leadership was part of its broader efforts to work with its flagbearer towards winning the 2028 general election. Mr Kodua also dismissed speculation about the selection of a running mate for the party’s flagbearer, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, saying the party had not taken a decision on the matter. Referring to Article 13 of the NPP constitution, he explained that the flagbearer was required to nominate a running mate in consultation with the National Council. He said the constitution did not provide for the selection of a running mate through a contest or campaign, warning party members and supporters against lobbying publicly for the position “Indeed, in selecting a running mate to our flagbearer, our constitution is very clear that the flagbearer, in consultation with the National Council, shall nominate the running mate. There is nowhere in our constitution that says that the running mate is selected through contest or through campaign. So people who are busily edging bloggers, edging people to promote them, the forum is wrong,” the General Secretary added.

items.title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Stablecoins here to optimise financial system, not replace it’
items.description: By Efosa Taiwo Stablecoins could transform cross-border payments by reducing transaction delays, improving liquidity and making money transfers faster and more accessible, speakers at Moonshot 2026 have said. The speakers made the remarks during a panel session titled “The New Payment Backbone: Stablecoins as Core Infrastructure for Global Liquidity” on the Emerging Tech Stage, where industry leaders discussed how stablecoins could reshape payments across Africa and the global financial system. Mercy Emmanuel, Stablecoin & Blockchain Vertical Lead, Flutterwave, said stablecoins could simplify international transfers, which often involve multiple intermediaries and take several days to complete. “Sending money from Lagos to Nairobi goes through a lot. It could take two to five days before it gets to its destination. Stablecoins collapse all these,” Emmanuel said. She likened the technology to a moving train that operates without the restrictions of banking hours and time zones, arguing that it could make payments almost instantaneous and allow businesses to conduct transactions seamlessly alongside their online operations. According to her, stablecoins could also encourage businesses to rethink their payment processes and build more efficient financial operations. “Stablecoins are here to optimise the financial system, not displace the traditional way,” she said, adding that the financial industry was moving towards a system in which the focus would be on how quickly and efficiently money could move from one point to another. Tayo Oviosu, Group Chief Executive Officer of Paga, said widespread stablecoin adoption would require collaboration among financial technology companies, sufficient liquidity and simpler access for everyday users. He argued that consumers were more concerned about the cost and speed of financial services than the underlying technology powering their transactions. “Ultimately, it is giving them what they want: they want to go from fiat to fiat. Stablecoin can be used in between,” he said. Oviosu added that solving liquidity challenges would make stablecoin transactions easier to access and use, stressing that no single company could independently make the technology a mainstream part of everyday financial life. “We want to make it simple. The way you can come to Paga and get a naira wallet, get a stablecoin wallet. That is the part of the user,” he said. He also called for industry players to work together to expand the use of stablecoins, noting that stronger collaboration would be necessary to improve access to the infrastructure and liquidity required to support wider adoption. Ife Johnson, co-founder of JuicyWay, also emphasised the need for shared infrastructure, urging industry players to move away from isolated systems towards solutions that could support the wider financial ecosystem. “The mind shift that needs to happen is moving from silos to shared infrastructure for industry players,” Johnson said. On regulation, Johnson said collaboration between businesses and regulators would be critical to ensuring the technology could develop responsibly. He noted that adoption could take time because of the broader implications of introducing new payment systems into existing financial structures. He expressed confidence that demonstrating responsible implementation and addressing potential concerns would help build regulatory trust and encourage progress. Oviosu also pointed to changing conversations around stablecoins and digital payments in Nigeria, saying engagement between industry stakeholders and regulators had become increasingly encouraging. “Three, four years ago, who could have said CBN will support stablecoins, NCC welcomes the idea? It is interesting to see that dialogue,” he said. He added that Nigeria could help set an example for other African markets if stakeholders maintained constructive engagement and worked together to address the challenges surrounding adoption. Emmanuel similarly welcomed what she described as growing support from the Federal Government, saying cooperation among industry participants and policymakers would be important to the development of the ecosystem. items.title: Grealish dropped for Everton’s League Cup tie after disciplinary breach
items.description: Jack Grealish was dropped for Everton’s League Cup fourth round clash against Newcastle on Thursday after “a breach of club discipline”. It was reported that the breach related to Grealish’s unauthorised absence from training. The 31-year-old missed Saturday’s 2-0 loss at Arsenal in the Premier League due to an illness. Grealish, who is on a second season-long loan from Manchester City, had started Everton’s three Premier League matches prior to their defeat against champions Arsenal. The 31-year-old has made six appearances for David Moyes’s side this term, most recently in their loss against Chelsea on October 17. Grealish has been dogged by criticism of his off-pitch behaviour for several years amid reports of nightclub incidents that saw him fall out of favour at City. After playing a key role in City’s treble-winning campaign in 2022-23, Grealish became an increasingly sidelined figure at the Etihad Stadium. Everton are facing Newcastle for a place in the League Cup quarter-finals, with Fleetwood awaiting the winner after their shock victory over Arsenal on Tuesday. items.title: Agadir : un policier percuté, une tentative de fuite et trois interpellations
items.description: Les éléments de police relevant de la préfecture de police d'Agadir ont interpellé, ce jeudi 29 octobre au matin, trois individus, dont le conducteur d'une voiture particulière et deux passagers qui l'accompagnaient. Ils sont soupçonnés d'être impliqués dans une affaire liée à l'état d'ivresse, au refus d'obtempérer et à des violences volontaires commises à l'encontre d'un agent de police dans l'exercice de ses fonctions, au cours d'une intervention sécuritaire ayant entraîné la blessure d'un policier évacué vers le Centre Hospitalier Universitaire (CHU) pour y recevoir les soins nécessaires. Selon les données préliminaires de l'enquête, les faits remontent au refus du conducteur du véhicule de se conformer à la sommation d'arrêt émise par les éléments de police chargés du contrôle au niveau du barrage judiciaire dressé à l'entrée nord de la ville d'Agadir. L'automobiliste a poursuivi sa route sans respecter les instructions sécuritaires, ce qui a exigé l'intervention d'une patrouille mobile qui a réussi à intercepter le véhicule au niveau de l'avenue Mohammed V dans le cadre des procédures visant à interpeller le chauffeur et à vérifier les motifs de son refus d'obtempérer. Lors de la procédure d'interpellation, le conducteur a délibérément percuté à deux reprises l'un des fonctionnaires de police avec sa voiture avant de tenter de faire marche arrière pour s'enfuir du lieu de l'accident et échapper à l'action des forces de l'ordre. Les éléments de sécurité sont parvenus à maîtriser rapidement la situation et à intercepter le mis en cause ainsi que ses deux passagers, ces derniers ayant été interpellés en état d'ivresse. À la suite de cet incident, le policier blessé a été transféré au CHU d'Agadir afin de subir les examens médicaux requis et de recevoir le traitement adéquat. Parallèlement, les trois suspects ont été placés en garde à vue sous la supervision du parquet compétent dans l'attente de la finalisation des procédures légales applicables. Les enquêteurs poursuivent leurs investigations afin de déterminer l'ensemble des circonstances entourant cette affaire et d'établir avec précision les actes criminels imputables à chacun des interpellés à la lumière des résultats de l'enquête judiciaire en cours. items.title: PLF 2027 : 9,21 MMDH pour explorer de nouveaux gisements de pétrole et de gaz
items.description: Le Maroc prévoit de mobiliser 9,21 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) entre 2026 et 2031 pour intensifier l’exploration des hydrocarbures. Selon le rapport sur les établissements et entreprises publics accompagnant le projet de loi de finances (PLF) 2027, ce programme reposera principalement sur les financements des partenaires, tandis que l’épuisement progressif des réserves gazières du bassin du Gharb renforce la nécessité de découvrir de nouveaux gisements. Le Maroc entend accélérer la recherche de nouvelles ressources pétrolières et gazières à travers un programme d’investissement de 9,21 MMDH sur la période 2026-2031. Portée par l’Office national des hydrocarbures et des mines (ONHYM), cette initiative vise à intensifier les opérations de prospection, à élargir les zones couvertes par les travaux d’exploration et à attirer de nouveaux investisseurs spécialisés dans les hydrocarbures. D’après le rapport sur les établissements et entreprises publics annexé au projet de loi de finances 2027, les partenaires devraient financer près de 91% des investissements prévus, soit environ 8,38 MMDH. La contribution directe de l’Office est estimée à 829 millions de dirhams (MDH). Ce modèle permet de répartir les coûts d’exploration avec les entreprises partenaires, dans un secteur où les opérations de recherche et de forage nécessitent des moyens importants sans garantir systématiquement la découverte de réserves commercialement exploitables. L’ONHYM mène actuellement ses activités d’exploration des hydrocarbures en partenariat avec onze entreprises, sur une superficie totale de 107.870,91 km². Ce périmètre comprend dix permis terrestres, trente permis offshore, deux autorisations de reconnaissance en mer et trois concessions d’exploitation. Un financement largement assuré par les partenaires La place prépondérante des financements extérieurs s’est également vérifiée en 2025. Les investissements consacrés à l’exploration pétrolière ont atteint 395 MDH, dont 370 millions apportés par les partenaires, contre 25 MDH provenant des ressources propres de l’Office. Au cours de la même période, l’établissement a signé dix-neuf accords destinés à encourager de nouveaux partenariats et procédé au forage d’un puits d’exploration terrestre. Les contributions des partenaires ont ainsi représenté environ 93,7% des investissements pétroliers réalisés en 2025, une proportion supérieure à celle prévue pour le programme 2026-2031. L’Office entend poursuivre cette stratégie afin de financer les opérations de recherche aussi bien à terre qu’en mer et d’augmenter les possibilités d’identification de nouveaux gisements. Le recul des réserves gazières accélère la recherche La nécessité de renouveler les ressources disponibles apparaît également dans les chiffres de production. En 2025, les volumes de gaz naturel livrés au titre de la part de l’ONHYM ont reculé de 21% sur un an, à 20,14 millions de mètres cubes normaux. Le rapport attribue cette baisse à l’épuisement progressif des réserves du bassin du Gharb et à l’absence de nouveaux forages. Les quantités de condensats livrées ont également diminué, d’environ 10%, pour s’établir à 1.729,76 tonnes. Ces évolutions soulignent les difficultés liées au maintien de la production des gisements actuellement exploités et la nécessité d’intensifier les travaux géologiques et les forages d’exploration. En parallèle, le volume de gaz naturel transitant par le gazoduc Maghreb-Europe a progressé de 7,9% en 2025, pour atteindre environ 890,1 millions de mètres cubes normaux, soit 10,37 milliards de kilowattheures. La société OUMCO, filiale de l’ONHYM, assure l’exploitation et la maintenance de cette infrastructure. L’exploration minière également au programme Les activités de l’Office ne se limitent pas aux hydrocarbures. Les travaux d’exploration minière réalisés en 2025 ont couvert plus de 7.000 km², pour des investissements de 724,5 MDH, financés à hauteur de 87,25% par les partenaires. Pour la période 2026-2028, l’ONHYM prévoit un programme de cinquante projets d’exploration minière. Vingt-sept seront développés avec ses propres moyens et vingt-trois dans le cadre de partenariats. Les recherches porteront notamment sur les métaux précieux et stratégiques, l’hydrogène naturel et de nouvelles ressources énergétiques. L’Office prévoit également d’évaluer le potentiel national en matière de stockage géologique de l’énergie et du dioxyde de carbone. Sur le plan financier, le chiffre d’affaires de l’établissement s’est élevé à 507,5 millions de dirhams en 2025, en hausse de 6% par rapport à 2024. Son résultat net a toutefois fortement reculé, passant de 95,55 à 2,77 MDH. À fin juin 2026, le chiffre d’affaires atteignait 215 MDH. Les prévisions pour l’ensemble de l’année tablent sur 634 MDH de recettes et un résultat net positif de 85 MDH. Les investissements devraient s’établir à 386 MDH, contre 636 millions initialement programmés dans le cadre de la loi de finances 2026. Pour 2027, le chiffre d’affaires prévisionnel est fixé à 686 MDH, avant de revenir à 655 millions en 2028, puis à 567 millions en 2029. Le projet de loi de finances 2027 prévoit, de son côté, 409 MDH d’investissements pour l’Office. Une nouvelle organisation et le projet de gazoduc africain Cette programmation intervient alors que l’ONHYM engage une nouvelle étape de son évolution institutionnelle. La loi n° 56.24 portant transformation de l’établissement en société anonyme a été publiée le 15 juin 2026. Cette réforme vise à faire évoluer son fonctionnement et à accompagner les transformations du secteur énergétique. L’Office participe également au développement du projet de gazoduc africain atlantique, en partenariat avec la Nigerian National Petroleum Company. Selon le rapport, les États membres de la Communauté économique des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (Cédéao) ont signé, le 19 juillet dernier à Freetown, l’accord intergouvernemental encadrant le développement du projet. L’infrastructure envisagée devrait s’étendre sur près de 6.800 kilomètres, avec une capacité de transport estimée à 30 milliards de mètres cubes de gaz par an. Elle doit permettre d’approvisionner treize pays de la façade atlantique africaine avant d’être raccordée au gazoduc Maghreb-Europe. Les premières opérations d’approvisionnement sont envisagées à l’horizon 2031. items.title: Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse « Dakar 2026 »: 136 athlètes, un même rêve de gloire
items.description: Le compte à rebours est lancé. Avec 136 athlètes engagés dans 23 disciplines, le Sénégal s’apprête à vivre un moment historique en accueillant les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (Joj) pour la première fois sur son sol. Une participation ambitieuse, portée par une jeunesse déterminée à faire honneur aux couleurs nationales. À partir du samedi 31 octobre, les Joj « Dakar 2026 » s’ouvriront pour deux semaines de compétition. Au total, 2 700 athlètes venus du monde entier s’affronteront dans 25 disciplines, avec l’ambition de décrocher des médailles et de faire briller les couleurs de leurs pays. Du côté de la délégation sénégalaise, la confiance est de mise et la motivation est palpable. Derrière les 136 athlètes qualifiés se trouvent des mois d’entraînement, des sacrifices et une volonté commune de se montrer à la hauteur de l’événement. Ces Joj représentent bien plus qu’une simple compétition. Ils offrent à ces jeunes l’occasion de défendre les couleurs nationales devant leur public, de se mesurer aux meilleurs talents mondiaux de leur génération et de démontrer que le Sénégal a toute sa place parmi les nations montantes du sport. Les attentes sont fortes. Le public espère des performances, des exploits et des moments de fierté. Les athlètes en sont conscients et entendent transformer cette pression en une source de motivation supplémentaire. À domicile, ils auront l’avantage de bénéficier du soutien populaire, mais aussi la responsabilité de porter les espoirs de toute une nation. Accueillir les premiers Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse organisés en Afrique constitue une étape majeure pour le Sénégal et pour le continent. Au-delà de la compétition, cet événement offre au pays une occasion exceptionnelle de mettre en lumière ses talents, de valoriser son savoir-faire organisationnel et de réaffirmer son engagement en faveur de la jeunesse et du sport. Pour les jeunes sénégalais, l’enjeu est de transformer les efforts consentis en résultats concrets et les rêves en ambitions durables. Chaque épreuve sera une occasion de se révéler, d’acquérir de l’expérience et de poser les premières pierres d’une carrière sportive prometteuse. Dans cette quête, les athlètes ne seront pas seuls. Entraîneurs, fédérations, familles et supporters auront un rôle essentiel à jouer pour les accompagner, les encourager et les pousser à donner le meilleur d’eux-mêmes. La réussite de cette aventure dépendra aussi de cette mobilisation collective autour des représentants du Sénégal. 136 athlètes, 23 disciplines, une seule ambition : faire briller le Sénégal. Le défi est immense, mais les espoirs sont à la hauteur de l’événement. Une jeunesse motivée, des talents à révéler et tout un pays derrière ses représentants. Autant d’atouts pour aborder ce rendez-vous avec détermination. À Dakar, Diamniadio et Saly, l’heure n’est plus seulement aux discours. Elle est à la mobilisation, à l’engagement et à la performance. Les Joj « Dakar 2026 » offrent à cette génération une occasion unique de marquer l’histoire du sport sénégalais. Le Sénégal rêve grand. À sa jeunesse désormais de saisir cette chance, de se dépasser et d’écrire, avec courage et ambition, une nouvelle page de son histoire sportive. Par Samba Oumar FALL
